FC stands for "'''F'''ootbal '''C'''lub". is a professional [[Association football|football]] club. It is based in [[Old Trafford (area)|Old Trafford]], [[Greater Manchester]], [[England]]. It plays in the [[Premier League]], the highest level of [[English football league system|English football]]. Its [[nickname]] is "the Red Devils". The club started as Newton Heath LYR Football Club, in 1878. It changed its name to Manchester United in 1902. It moved to its current [[stadium]], [[Old Trafford]], in 1910. Manchester United has won more [[Trophy|trophies]] than any other club in English football other than Liverpool FC.{{cite web|last=Smith|first=Adam|date=30 November 2016|title=Leeds United England's 12th biggest club, according to Sky Sports study|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11715/10676765/leeds-united-englands-13th-biggest-club-according-to-sky-sports-study|work=Sky Sports}}{{Cite news|last=McNulty|first=Phil|date=21 September 2012|title=Liverpool v Manchester United: The bitter rivalry|work=BBC Sports|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19653230}} It has won 20 [[Premier League|League titles]], 13 [[FA Cup|FA Cups]], six [[EFL Cup|League Cups]] and 21 [[FA Community Shield|FA Community Shields]]. United has also won three [[UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions Leagues]], one [[UEFA Europa League]], one [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup]], one [[UEFA Super Cup]], one [[Intercontinental Cup (football)|Intercontinental Cup]] and one [[FIFA Club World Cup]]. In [[1998–99 Manchester United F.C. season|1998–99]], the club became the first club in the history of English football to win the [[Treble (association football)|continental European treble]].{{cite news|title=BBC ON THIS DAY – 14 – 1969: Matt Busby retires from Man United|work=BBC News|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/onthisday/hi/dates/stories/january/14/newsid_3334000/3334059.stm}} It won the UEFA Europa League in [[2016–17 Manchester United F.C. season|2016–17]] and became [[UEFA club competition records and statistics#List of teams to have won the three main European club competitions|one of five clubs]] to win all three top [[UEFA]] club competitions. [[Matt Busby]] led the club to lots of success by using youth players until the [[Munich air disaster]] in 1958. The Munich air disaster is a famous plane [[Accident|crash]] in the club's history. Eight Manchester United players died as well as other staff. In 1968, the manager Matt Busby guided Manchester United to the European Cup. It became the first English football club to win this trophy. [[Alex Ferguson|Sir Alex Ferguson]] is one of the most famous managers of the club. He won 38 trophies as manager. This includes 13 Premier League titles, five FA Cups and two UEFA Champions Leagues, between 1986 and 2013.{{cite news|date=8 May 2013|title=The 49 trophies of Sir Alex Ferguson – the most successful managerial career Britain has ever known|work=The Independent|publisher=Independent Print|location=London|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/the-49-trophies-of-sir-alex-ferguson-the-most-successful-managerial-career-britain-has-ever-known-8607136.html|accessdate=30 October 2015}}{{cite news|last=Stewart|first=Rob|date=1 October 2009|title=Sir Alex Ferguson successful because he was given time, says Steve Bruce|work=The Daily Telegraph|location=London|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/manchester-united/6250406/Sir-Alex-Ferguson-successful-because-he-was-given-time-says-Steve-Bruce.html|accessdate=11 May 2011}}{{cite news|last=Northcroft|first=Jonathan|date=5 November 2006|title=20 glorious years, 20 key decisions|work=The Sunday Times|publisher=Times Newspapers|location=London|url=http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/sport/football/article625585.ece|accessdate=24 June 2010|archive-date=9 March 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070309065821/http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/sport/football/article625585.ece|url-status=dead}} He [[Retirement|retired]] in 2013. Manchester United was [[Stock market|floated]] on the [[London Stock Exchange]] in 1991. [[Malcolm Glazer]] bought the club in May 2005. This valued the club at almost £800 million. After this, the company became private again. In August 2012, it went public once more. It made an [[initial public offering]] on the [[New York Stock Exchange]]. Manchester United was the [[Deloitte Football Money League|highest-earning]] football club in the world in 2016–17. It had an annual [[revenue]] of €676.3 million.{{cite news|last=Wilson|first=Bill|date=23 January 2018|title=Manchester United remain football's top revenue-generator|publisher=BBC News (British Broadcasting Corporation)|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-42767374|accessdate=14 April 2018}} It was the most [[Value|valuable]] football club in the world in 2024.{{Cite web|last=Prenn|first=Tamara|date=2024-05-08|title=Revealed: Manchester United is world's most valuable football club|url=https://www.dailymail.co.uk/sport/football/article-13396115/Man-United-valuable-football-club-4-9BILLION.html|access-date=2024-05-18|website=Mail Online}} Its value was £4.96 billion ($6.2 billion). As of June 2015, it is also the world's most valuable football [[wikt:brand|brand]]. Its [[Estimation|estimated]] value is $1.2 billion.{{cite news|date=8 June 2015|title=Manchester United is 'most valuable football brand'|publisher=BBC News (British Broadcasting Corporation)|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-33044663|accessdate=8 June 2015}}{{cite web|last=Schwartz|first=Peter J.|date=18 April 2012|title=Manchester United Again The World's Most Valuable Soccer Team|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/mikeozanian/2012/04/18/manchester-united-again-the-worlds-most-valuable-soccer-team/|work=Forbes Magazine|accessdate=5 May 2012}} Manchester United has the most fans in the world.Hamil (2008), p. 126.[http://www.marca.com/en/2014/11/13/en/football/barcelona/1415913827.html "Barça, the most loved club in the world"]. Marca. Retrieved 15 December 2014 It has big [[Rival|rivalries]] with [[Liverpool F.C.]], [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] and [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]]. == History == === Early years (1878–1945) === Manchester United was started in 1878. It was called '''Newton Heath LYR Football Club'''. The [[Carriage]] and [[Wagon]] [[Departmentalisation|department]] of the [[Lancashire and Yorkshire Railway]] (LYR) [[depot]] started the club at [[Newton Heath]].Barnes et al. (2001), p. 8. All of the team worked at [[Lancashire and Yorkshire Railway]] depot. The team first played against other departments and against other [[Rail transport|railway]] companies. On 20 November 1880, it played in their first official match. The players wore the colours of the railway company: green and gold. They lost 6–0 against the [[reserve team]] of [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]].James (2008), p. 66. In 1888, the club became a [[wikt:found|founding]] member of [[The Combination]], a regional football league. The league stopped after only one year. Newton Heath joined the new [[Football Alliance]]. This ran for three seasons. It was then [[wikt:combine|combined]] with The Football League. This meant the club started the 1892–93 season in the [[Football League First Division|First Division]]. By this time it was not a part of the railway company. It did not use "LYR" in its name anymore. After two seasons, the club was [[Promotion and relegation|relegated]] to the [[Football League Second Division|Second Division]]. [[File:Man.utd_1905-06_dailygraph.jpg|alt=A black-and-white photograph of a football team lining up before a match. Four players, wearing dark shirts, light shorts and dark socks, are seated. Four more players are standing immediately behind them, and three more are standing on a higher level on the back row. Two men in suits are standing on either side of the players.|left|thumb|The Manchester United team at the start of the [[1905–06 Manchester United F.C. season|1905–06 season]], in which they were runners-up in the Second Division]] In January 1902 the club had [[Debt|debts]] of £2,670, equivalent to (the same as) £{{formatnum:{{Inflation|UK|2670|1902|r=-4}}|0}} in {{CURRENTYEAR}}.{{Inflation-fn|UK|group=nb}} The club got a [[wikt:liquidation|winding-up order]].Tyrrell & Meek (1996), p. 99. Captain [[Harry Stafford]] found four local businessmen, including [[John Henry Davies]] who became club president. Each businessman invested £500. They were then allowed to help run the club. On 24 April 1902, they changed the name of the club to '''Manchester United F.C.'''.Barnes et al. (2001), p. 9.James (2008), p. 92.Sources are divided on the exact date of the meeting and subsequent name change. Whilst official club sources claim that it occurred on 26 April, the meeting was reported by the ''Manchester Evening Chronicle'' in its edition of 25 April, suggesting it was indeed on 24 April. [[Ernest Mangnall]] became the manager in 1903. The team finished the Second Division in second position in 1906. It went back to the First Division. It won the league in 1908. This was the club's first league title. The season after, the club won the first ever [[FA Community Shield|Charity Shield]].Barnes et al. (2001), p. 118. That season, the club also won its first FA Cup title. Manchester United won the First Division for the second time in 1911. At the end of the next season, Mangnall left the club to join [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]].Barnes et al. (2001), p. 11. In 1922, three years after football started again after the First World War, the club was relegated to the Second Division. It stayed in this division until 1925. It went back to the first division, but was relegated again in 1931. Manchester United became a [[yo-yo club]]. In 1934 it had its worst ever position in the league. It was 20th place in the Second Division. The main [[Sponsor|benefactor]], John Henry Davies, died in October 1927. After this the club's finances got worse. Manchester United were close to [[bankruptcy]], but [[James W. Gibson]] [[Investment|invested]] £2,000 in December 1931.Barnes et al. (2001), p. 12. He took control of the club. In the [[1938–39 Manchester United F.C. season|1938–39 season]], the last year of football before the Second World War, the club was 14th in the First Division. === Busby years (1945–1969) === [[File:Busby_babes_1955.jpg|alt=A black-and-white photograph of several people in suits and overcoats on the steps of an aircraft.|thumb|The Busby Babes in Denmark in 1955]] In October 1945, football started again. [[Matt Busby]] became the manager. He wanted a lot of control when choosing payers, player [[Transfer (association football)|transfers]] and training [[wikt:session|sessions]].Barnes et al. (2001), p. 13. Busby and his team finished second in 1947, 1948 and 1949. They won the FA Cup in 1948. In 1952, the club won the First Division. This was the first time that it won the league for 41 years.Barnes et al. (2001), p. 10. It also won league titles in 1956 and 1957. Matt Busby used the youth team to get new players, and this was very successful. At that time, the team had [[average]] age of 22. The [[News|media]] gave them the nickname "the Busby Babes". This was because Busby believed in his young players.Murphy (2006), p. 71. In 1957, Manchester United became the first English team to play in the European Cup. The Football League did not want the club to play, but it did not stop them. The year before, the Football League had stopped [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] from playing in that cup.{{cite news|last=Glanville|first=Brian|date=27 April 2005|title=The great Chelsea surrender|work=The Times|publisher=Times Newspapers|location=London|url=http://www.timesonline.co.uk/article/0,,762-1586242,00.html|accessdate=24 June 2010|archive-date=5 August 2011|archive-url=https://archive.today/20110805092558/http://www.timesonline.co.uk/article/0,,762-1586242,00.html|url-status=dead}} United lost in the semi-final to [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]]. However, earlier in the tournament the team won 10–0 victory against Belgian champions [[R.S.C. Anderlecht|Anderlecht]]. This is still the club's biggest ever victory.Barnes et al. (2001), pp. 14–15. [[File:Munich_air_disaster_plaque.jpg|alt=A stone tablet, inscribed with the image of a football pitch and several names. It is surrounded by a stone border in the shape of a football stadium. Above the tablet is a wooden carving of two men holding a large wreath.|left|thumb|A plaque at Old Trafford in memory of those who died in the Munich air disaster, including players' names]] The season after, the [[Munich air disaster]] happened. It was after the club won against [[Red Star Belgrade]] in the European Cup quarter-final. The plane carrying the Manchester United players, officials and journalists crashed while trying to [[Takeoff|take off]] after it stopped for [[fuel]] in [[Munich]], [[Germany]]. 23 people died in the [[Munich air disaster]] of 6 February 1958. This included eight players: [[Geoff Bent]], [[Roger Byrne]], [[Eddie Colman]], [[Duncan Edwards]], [[Mark Jones (footballer, born 1933)|Mark Jones]], [[David Pegg]], [[Tommy Taylor]] and [[Billy Whelan]]. The crash also [[Injury|injured]] many other people.{{cite news|date=6 February 1958|title=1958: United players killed in air disaster|work=BBC News|publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/onthisday/hi/dates/stories/february/6/newsid_2535000/2535961.stm|accessdate=24 June 2010}}Barnes et al. (2001), pp. 16–17. [[File:WillemIIManchesterUnited1963c.jpg|thumb|Manchester United (1963)]] The assistant manager, [[Jimmy Murphy (footballer)|Jimmy Murphy]], became the manager while Busby [[wikt:recover|recovered]] from his injuries. The club still got to the [[1958 FA Cup Final|FA Cup final]], but it lost to [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]]. In [[wikt:recognition|recognition]] of the team's [[wikt:tragedy|tragedy]], [[UEFA]] invited the club to play in the [[1958–59 European Cup]]. The Football Association agreed, but the Football League said that the club should not enter the competition, because it had not qualified.White, Jim (2008), p. 136.Barnes et al. (2001), p. 17. Busby built the team again in the 1960s. He signed players such as [[Denis Law]] and [[Pat Crerand]]. They played well with the next generation of young players, including [[George Best]]. The club won the FA Cup in [[1963 FA Cup Final|1963]]. The season after, it finished second in the league. It won the league in 1965 and 1967. In 1968, Manchester United became the first English (and second British, after [[Celtic F.C.]]) club to win the European Cup. It beat [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] 4–1 in the [[1968 European Cup Final|final]].Barnes et al. (2001), pp. 18–19. The team had three [[Ballon d'Or (1956–2009)|European Footballers of the Year]]: [[Bobby Charlton]], Denis Law and George Best.{{cite web|last1=Moore|first1=Rob|last2=Stokkermans|first2=Karel|date=11 December 2009|title=European Footballer of the Year ("Ballon d'Or")|url=http://www.rsssf.com/miscellaneous/europa-poy.html|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|accessdate=24 June 2010}} The club then [[wikt:represent|represented]] [[Europe]] in the [[1968 Intercontinental Cup]] against [[Club Estudiantes de La Plata|Estudiantes]] of [[Argentina]]. It lost the first match in [[Buenos Aires]], 1–0. It drew 1–1 at Old Trafford three weeks later. This meant Manchester United lost the cup. Busby [[Resignation|resigned]] as manager in 1969. The reserve team coach replaced him. He was former Manchester United player [[Wilf McGuinness]].Barnes et al. (2001), p. 19. === 1969–1986 === [[File:Bryan_Robson_at_the_cliff_-march_92.JPG|alt=A smiling man with dark hair wearing a white, green and blue tracksuit top over a blue shirt. He is holding a washbag under his right arm.|thumb|[[Bryan Robson]] was the captain of Manchester United for 12 years, longer than any other player.Barnes et al. (2001), p. 110.]] The club finished in 8th place in the [[1969–70 Manchester United F.C. season|1969–70 season]]. It had a bad start to the [[1970–71 Manchester United F.C. season|1970–71 season]]. Busby started to be the [[wikt:temporary|temporary]] manager again. McGuinness went back to be the reserve team coach. In June 1971, [[Frank O'Farrell]] became the manager. He stayed less than 18 months. [[Tommy Docherty]] became the new manager in December 1972.Murphy (2006), p. 134. Docherty helped Manchester United stay in the First Division that season. However, the club relegated to the second division in 1974. Best, Law, and Charlton had left the club by that point.Barnes et al. (2001), pp. 18–19. The team won promotion back to the first division theyear after. United played in the FA Cup final in [[1976 FA Cup Final|1976]], but [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] won the match. The club was in the final again in [[1977 FA Cup Final|1977]]. It beat [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] 2–1. Docherty was sacked soon after, because he had had an [[affair]] with the club [[Physiotherapy|physiotherapist's]] wife.Barnes et al. (2001), p. 19.{{cite news|date=4 July 1977|title=1977: Manchester United sack manager|work=BBC News|publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/onthisday/hi/dates/stories/july/4/newsid_2492000/2492743.stm|accessdate=2 April 2010}} [[Dave Sexton]] became the new manager in the summer of 1977. He signed the famous players [[Joe Jordan (footballer)|Joe Jordan]], [[Gordon McQueen]], [[Gary Bailey]], and [[Ray Wilkins]]. However, the team did not have great results. It finished in the top two in 1979–80. It lost against [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] in the [[1979 FA Cup Final]]. Sexton was sacked in 1981, even though the team won the last seven games when he was the manager.Barnes et al. (2001), p. 20. [[Ron Atkinson]] replaced him. He broke the British record transfer fee (the money used to buy a player) to sign [[Bryan Robson]] from [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]]. Under Atkinson, Manchester United won the FA Cup twice in three years – in [[1983 FA Cup Final|1983]] and [[1985 FA Cup Final|1985]]. In [[1985–86 Manchester United F.C. season|1985–86]], the club was favourite to win the league after 13 wins and two draws in its first 15 matches. However, they only finished the season in fourth place. Atkinson was sacked the year after, because the club was already in danger of relegation by November.Barnes et al. (2001), pp. 20–21. === Ferguson years (1986–2013) === [[File:Alex_Ferguson.jpg|alt=The torso and head of a grey-haired white man. He is wearing spectacles and a black coat.|left|thumb|[[Alex Ferguson]] managed the team between 1986 and 2013.]] [[Alex Ferguson]] and his assistant [[Archie Knox]] arrived from [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] on the day of Atkinson's left.Barnes et al. (2001), p. 21. They guided the club to an 11th-place finish in the league.Barnes et al. (2001), p. 148. They finished second in [[1987–88 Manchester United F.C. season|1987–88]], but the club was back in 11th place the season after.Barnes et al. (2001), pp. 148–149. [[Journalist|Reports]] say Ferguson almost lost his job. A win against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] in the [[1990 FA Cup Final]] replay (after a 3–3 draw) [[wikt:save|saved]] Ferguson's [[career]].{{cite news|date=27 May 1999|title=Arise Sir Alex?|work=BBC News|publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/special_report/1999/05/99/uniteds_treble_triumph/354282.stm|accessdate=2 April 2010}}{{cite news|last=Bevan|first=Chris|date=4 November 2006|title=How Robins saved Ferguson's job|work=BBC Sport|publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/m/man_utd/6096520.stm|accessdate=2 April 2010}} The season after this, Manchester United won its first [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup|Cup Winners' Cup]] title. It also played in the [[1991 European Super Cup|1991 UEFA Super Cup]]. It beat [[1990–91 European Cup|European Cup]] holders (the champions from the year before) [[Red Star Belgrade]] 1–0 in the final at Old Trafford. In 1992, United played in another League Cup final. The club beat Nottingham Forest 1–0 at Wembley.Barnes et al. (2001), pp. 20–21. In 1993, Manchester United won its first league title since 1967. A year later, for the first time since 1957, it won a second title in a row. It also won the FA Cup. This means the team completed the first "[[Double (association football)|Double]]" in the club's history. United then became the first English club to win the Double twice. It won both competitions again in 1995–96.{{cite web|last=161385360554578|date=4 May 2017|title=Clubs ranked by the number of times they have claimed trophy doubles|url=https://talksport.com/football/fa-cup/228286/trophy-doubles-english-clubs-ranked-number-times-they-have-claimed-two-major-trophies-one/|publisher=}} In 1996–97, it won the league again, one game before the end of the season.{{cite news|date=22 April 2013|title=Golden years: The tale of Manchester United's 20 titles|work=BBC Sport|publisher=|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21878651}} [[File:The_Champions_League_Winners_Medal_(Manchester_United_Museum)_(262769292).jpg|thumb|Front three: Manchester United's [[Treble (association football)|treble]] medals of the [[1998–99 Manchester United F.C. season|1998–99 season]] are displayed at the club's museum.]] In the [[1998–99 Manchester United F.C. season|1998–99 season]], Manchester United became the first team to win the Premier League, FA Cup and UEFA Champions League – "The Treble" – in the same season.{{cite news|date=26 May 1999|title=United crowned kings of Europe|work=BBC Sport|publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/sport/football/353842.stm|accessdate=22 June 2010}} The team was losing 1–0 going into [[injury time]] in the [[1999 UEFA Champions League Final]]. [[Teddy Sheringham]] and [[Ole Gunnar Solskjær]] scored late goals to claim a [[wikt:dramatic|dramatic]] victory against [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]]. It is remembered as one of the greatest comebacks (when you were losing and came back to win) of all time.{{cite news|last=Hoult|first=Nick|date=28 August 2007|title=Ole Gunnar Solskjaer leaves golden memories|work=The Daily Telegraph|location=London|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/2320013/Ole-Gunnar-Solskjaer-leaves-golden-memories.html|accessdate=23 July 2011}} The club also won the Intercontinental Cup. It beat [[Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras|Palmeiras]] 1–0 in Tokyo.{{cite news|last1=Magnani|first1=Loris|last2=Stokkermans|first2=Karel|date=30 April 2005|title=Intercontinental Club Cup|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|url=http://www.rsssf.com/tablest/toyota.html|accessdate=24 June 2010}} Ferguson was then [[Knight Bachelor|knighted]] for his services to football.{{cite news|last=Hughes|first=Rob|date=8 March 2004|title=Ferguson and Magnier: a truce in the internal warfare at United|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/03/08/sports/08iht-stud_ed3_.html|accessdate=24 June 2010}} He became Sir Alex Ferguson. [[File:Ryan_Giggs_vs_Everton-5_cropped.jpg|alt=A white football player with short, dark, greying hair. He is wearing a red shirt, white shorts, white socks and white football boots. He is running and has puffed-out cheeks.|left|thumb|[[Ryan Giggs]] is the most decorated player in English football history.{{cite news|date=13 December 2009|title=Ryan Giggs wins 2009 BBC Sports Personality award|work=BBC Sport|publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/tv_and_radio/sports_personality_of_the_year/8410840.stm|accessdate=11 June 2010}}]] Manchester United won the league again in the [[1999–2000 FA Premier League|1999–2000]] and [[2000–01 FA Premier League|2000–01]] seasons. The team finished third in [[2001–02 FA Premier League|2001–02]]. It won the title again in [[2002–03 FA Premier League|2002–03]].{{cite news|date=4 May 2003|title=Viduka hands title to Man Utd|publisher=BBC Sport (British Broadcasting Corporation)|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/2968015.stm|accessdate=14 August 2014}} It won the [[2004 FA Cup Final|2003–04 FA Cup]]. United beat [[Millwall F.C.|Millwall]] 3–0 in the final at the [[Millennium Stadium]] in [[Cardiff]]. It won the trophy for a record 11th time.{{cite news|date=22 May 2004|title=Man Utd win FA Cup|work=BBC Sport|publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/fa_cup/3725063.stm|accessdate=9 July 2010}} In the [[2005–06 Manchester United F.C. season|2005–06 season]], Manchester United did not play in the [[Knockout tournament|knockout phase]] of the UEFA Champions League. This was the first time in over ten years.{{cite news|date=8 December 2011|title=Manchester United's Champions League exits, 1993–2011|work=The Guardian|publisher=Guardian News and Media|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2011/dec/08/manchester-united-champions-league-exit|accessdate=14 August 2014}} The club still managed to finish second in the league. It also won the [[2006 Football League Cup Final]] against [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]]. The club won the Premier League again in the 2006–07 season. In 2007–08, it won the [[Double (association football)#European Doubles|European double]]. United won a [[penalty shootout]] 6–5 against Chelsea in the [[2008 UEFA Champions League Final]] in Moscow and won its 17th English league title. In that season, [[Ryan Giggs]] played a record 759th game for the club. This was more than the old record of Bobby Charlton.{{cite news|last=Shuttleworth|first=Peter|date=21 May 2008|title=Spot-on Giggs overtakes Charlton|work=BBC Sport|publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/m/man_utd/7411587.stm|accessdate=9 July 2010}} In December 2008, the club won the [[2008 FIFA Club World Cup]]. It then won the [[2008–09 Football League Cup]]. Later that year, United won a third Premier League title in a row.{{cite news|last=McNulty|first=Phil|date=1 March 2009|title=Man Utd 0–0 Tottenham (aet)|work=BBC Sport|publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/league_cup/7905889.stm|accessdate=1 March 2009}}{{cite news|last=McNulty|first=Phil|date=16 May 2009|title=Man Utd 0–0 Arsenal|work=BBC Sport|publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/8038259.stm|accessdate=16 May 2009}} In the summer of 2009, United sold [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] to Real Madrid for a [[world record]] £80 million.{{cite news|last=Ogden|first=Mark|date=12 June 2009|title=Cristiano Ronaldo transfer: World-record deal shows football is booming, says Sepp Blatter|work=The Daily Telegraph|location=London|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/manchester-united/5517910/Cristiano-Ronaldo-transfer-World-record-deal-shows-football-is-booming-says-Sepp-Blatter.html|accessdate=9 January 2011}} In 2010, Manchester United beat Aston Villa 2–1 at Wembley to win the [[2009–10 Football League Cup|League Cup]] again. This was the first time it defended (won again the next year) a knockout cup competition.{{cite news|date=28 February 2010|title=Rooney the hero as United overcome Villa|work=ESPNsoccernet|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=287675&cc=5739|url-status=dead|accessdate=2 April 2010|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100303090528/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=287675&cc=5739|archivedate=3 March 2010}} The club finished second behind Chelsea in the 2009–10 season. In 2010–11, United won a record 19th league title. It won the league with a 1–1 [[Road (sports)|away]] (at the [[wikt:opponent|opponent's]] [[stadium]]) draw against [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] on 14 May 2011.{{cite news|last=Stone|first=Simon|date=14 May 2011|title=Manchester United clinch record 19th English title|work=The Independent|publisher=Independent Print|location=London|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/manchester-united-clinch-record-19th-english-title-2284086.html|accessdate=14 May 2011}} It made this 20 league titles in 2012–13. It won the league with a 3–0 home (at their own stadium) win against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] on 22 April 2013.{{cite news|date=22 April 2013|title=How Manchester United won the 2012–13 Barclays Premier League|work=premierleague.com|publisher=Premier League|url=http://www.premierleague.com/en-gb/news/features/man-united-2012-13-season-at-a-glance.html|url-status=dead|accessdate=22 April 2013|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130425075443/http://www.premierleague.com/en-gb/news/features/man-united-2012-13-season-at-a-glance.html|archivedate=25 April 2013}} {| class="wikitable" align="right" |+'''Manchester United Name History''' !Years used !Name |- |1878-1892 |'''Newton Heath L&YR F.C.''' |- |1892-1902 |'''Newton Heath F.C.''' |- |1902-present |'''Manchester United F.C.''' |} === Recent history === ==== 2013 - Present ==== On 8 May 2013, Ferguson said he would [[Retirement|retire]] as manager at the end of the football season.{{cite news|date=8 May 2013|title=Sir Alex Ferguson to retire as Manchester United manager|work=BBC Sport|publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/22447018|accessdate=8 May 2013}}{{cite news|date=8 May 2013|title=Sir Alex Ferguson to retire this summer, Manchester United confirm|work=Sky Sports|publisher=BSkyB|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11667/8698530/Sir-Alex-Ferguson-to-retire-this-summer-Manchester-United-confirm|accessdate=8 May 2013}} He said he would stay at the club as a [[Board of directors|director]] and club [[ambassador]]. The club [[News release|announced]] the next day that [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] manager [[David Moyes]] would be the new manager from 1 July. He signed a six-year [[contract]].{{cite news|date=9 May 2013|title=David Moyes: Manchester United appoint Everton boss|work=BBC Sport|publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/22453802|accessdate=9 May 2013}}{{cite news|date=9 May 2013|title=Manchester United confirm appointment of David Moyes on a six-year contract|work=Sky Sports|publisher=BSkyB|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11671/8701469/Manchester-United-confirm-appointment-of-David-Moyes-on-a-six-year-contract|accessdate=9 May 2013}}{{cite news|last=Jackson|first=Jamie|date=9 May 2013|title=David Moyes quits as Everton manager to take over at Manchester United|work=guardian.co.uk|publisher=Guardian News and Media|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/may/09/david-moyes-quits-everton-manchester-united|accessdate=9 May 2013}} Moyes was sacked after a bad season.{{cite news|date=22 April 2014|title=David Moyes sacked by Manchester United after just 10 months in charge|newspaper=The Guardian|publisher=Guardian News and Media|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/apr/22/david-moyes-sacked-manchester-united|accessdate=22 April 2014}} The club finished 7th in the Premier League title. It did not qualify for the [[UEFA Champions League]] for the first time since 1995–96. The club also did not qualify for the Europa League. This was the first time Manchester United had not qualified for a European competition since 1990.{{cite news|last=Hassan|first=Nabil|date=11 May 2014|title=Southampton 1–1 Man Utd|publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/27273510|accessdate=29 May 2014}} [[Ryan Giggs]] became player-manager (when a player is also the manager at the same time) on 22 April 2014, only 10 months after Moyes became manager. On 19 May 2014, the club said [[Louis van Gaal]] would replace Moyes as Manchester United manager. He got a three-year deal. Giggs was his assistant.{{cite news|date=19 May 2014|title=Manchester United: Louis van Gaal confirmed as new manager|publisher=BBC Sport (British Broadcasting Corporation)|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/27243233|accessdate=29 May 2014}} [[Malcolm Glazer]], of the Glazer family that owns the club, died on 28 May 2014.{{cite news|last=Jackson|first=Jamie|date=28 May 2014|title=Manchester United owner Malcolm Glazer dies aged 86|newspaper=The Guardian|publisher=Guardian News and Media|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/may/28/malcolm-glazer-manchester-united-death-tampa-bay|accessdate=28 May 2014}} In Van Gaal's first season, United finished in fourth in the Premier League. This meant they reached the Champions League. In Van Gaal's second season, United lost in the group stage of this tournament.{{cite news|last=Wilkinson|first=Jack|date=9 December 2015|title=Wolfsburg 3–2 Man Utd: Champions League exit for van Gaal's men|publisher=Sky Sports (BSkyB)|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/wolfsburg-vs-man-utd/351420|accessdate=17 February 2016}} United bought a few expensive players. In 2015, after winning 3-0 against [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]], Man United reached 1st place for the first time in over two years. However, after losing 0-3 to [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], the club fell to 3rd place. The team did not do very well in the league. They finished in 5th place. However, that same season, Manchester United won the [[FA Cup]] for a 12th time. This was their first trophy since 2013.{{Cite news|last=Smith|first=Alan|date=21 May 2016|title=Crystal Palace 1–2 Manchester United (aet): FA Cup final – as it happened!|newspaper=The Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2016/may/21/crystal-palace-manchester-united-fa-cup-final-live|access-date=21 May 2016}} Van Gaal was sacked as manager just two days later.{{cite news|last1=Stone|first1=Simon|last2=Roan|first2=Dan|date=23 May 2016|title=Manchester United: Louis van Gaal sacked as manager|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36356584|accessdate=23 May 2016}} [[José Mourinho]] became the new manager on 27 May 2016. He signed a three-year contract.{{cite news|date=27 May 2016|title=Jose Mourinho: Man Utd confirm former Chelsea boss as new manager|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36363365|accessdate=27 May 2016}} That season, United finished in sixth place in the league. They won the [[2016–17 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] for the fifth time and the [[2016–17 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] for the first time. They also won the [[FA Community Shield]] for a record 21st time. This was Mourinho's first competitive (in a competition) match as the manager.{{cite news|last=Veevers|first=Nicholas|date=7 August 2016|title=United lift Shield after late Zlatan Ibrahimovic winner|website=TheFA.com|publisher=The Football Association|url=http://www.thefa.com/news/2016/aug/07/leicester-city-manchester-united-report-070816|accessdate=20 November 2019}} United didn not finish in the top four, but qualified for the Champions League because they won the Europa League. [[Wayne Rooney]] scored his 250th goal with United. He passed Sir Bobby Charlton as United's all-time top scorer. Rooney left the club at the end of the season. He went back to Everton. On 18 December 2018, Mourinho was sacked by the club after 144 games as the manager. United were in sixth place in the Premier League table. They were 19 points behind leaders Liverpool and 11 points outside the Champions League places (the top four). The day after, former Manchester United striker [[Ole Gunnar Solskjær|Ole Gunnar Solskær]] became the [[caretaker manager]] until the end of the season.{{Cite news|date=20 December 2018|title=Ole Gunnar Solskjaer: Man Utd caretaker boss will 'get players enjoying football' again|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46640577|access-date=21 December 2018}} On 28 March 2019, Solskjær became the permanent manager on a three-year deal.{{cite news|title=Ole Gunnar Solskjaer appointed Manchester United permanent manager|publisher=Sky Sports|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11667/11676599/ole-gunnar-solskjaer-appointed-manchester-united-permanent-manager|accessdate=28 March 2019}} Until then, he had 14 wins from his first 19 matches as manager. In this time, his team beat Paris Saint-Germain 3-1 in the Champions League after losing the first match 2-0. In the 2019-2020 season, Manchester United reached three semi-finals. They played in the semi-final of the League Cup, the FA Cup and the Europa league. They lost all three matches. This is the first time an English team has lost three cup semi-finals in the same season.{{Cite web|date=2020-08-17|title=Semi finals not acceptable for Manchester United, says Maguire|url=https://www.itv.com/news/granada/2020-08-17/semi-finals-not-acceptable-for-manchester-united-maguire|access-date=2020-08-18|website=ITV News|language=en}} Manchester United finished third in the Premier League. They beat Leicester City 2-0 in the last match of the season to stay above Chelsea who finished fourth.{{Cite news|date=2020-07-26|title=Leicester City 0-2 Manchester United: Visitors secure Champions League place|language=en-gb|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53460592|access-date=2020-08-18}} In January, the club signed midfield player [[Bruno Fernandes]].{{Cite news|date=2020-01-30|title=Bruno Fernandes: Manchester United sign Sporting Lisbon midfielder|language=en-gb|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51292312|access-date=2020-08-18}} He came from Portuguese club [[Sporting Lisbon]], like Cristiano Ronaldo 16 years before. The British media said that Fernandes was one of the main reasons the club finished in the top 4. {{Cite news|date=2020-06-30|title=Bruno Fernandes: How Man Utd gloom has been lifted by the Portuguese midfielder|language=en-gb|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53244336|access-date=2020-08-18}}{{Cite web|last=Collins|first=Jack|date=2020-03-10|title=Bruno Fernandes hailed as 'missing link' after 'changing whole Man Utd team'|url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/bruno-fernandes-hailed-missing-link-21667554|access-date=2020-08-18|website=mirror}} Manchester United did not lose in the Premier league for the rest of the season, after Fernandes joined (9 wins, 5 draws).{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Manchester United Premier League Statistics|url=https://www.premierleague.com/clubs/12/Manchester-United/results?co=1&se=274|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=18 August 2020|website=Premier League Official Website}} On 18 April 2021, Manchester United said it was joining 11 other European clubs to make a [[European Super League]] (ESL). This was going to be a 20-team competition to rival the UEFA Champions League.{{cite news |title=Leading football clubs announce new Super League competition |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/leading-football-clubs-announce-new-super-league-competition-18-april-2021 |work=Manchester United |date=18 April 2021 |access-date=19 January 2022 |archive-date=19 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210419133610/https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/leading-football-clubs-announce-new-super-league-competition-18-april-2021 |url-status=live }} Many fans, other clubs, media partners, sponsors, players and the [[Government of the United Kingdom|UK Government]] were very unhappy. The club changed its plans just two days later.{{Cite web |url=https://thebusbybabe.sbnation.com/2021/4/20/22394177/manchester-united-figures-react-to-super-league-news |title=Manchester United figures react to Super League news |first=Vince |last=Rosetta |date=20 April 2021 |website=The Busby Babe |access-date=29 June 2021 |archive-date=29 June 2021 vice-chairman [[Ed Woodward]] [[Resignation|resigned]] from his job. After the ESL plan, there were [[2021 Old Trafford protests|protests]] against Woodward and the Glazer family. There was a pitch invasion before a league match against Liverpool on 2 May 2021. This was the first time a match was moved in the Premier League game due to fan protests.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/manchester-united/story/4365318/woodward-out-as-manchester-united-executive-vice-chairman|title=Woodward resigns as Man United vice-chairman|date=20 April 2021|website=ESPN.com|access-date=29 June 2021|archive-date=29 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210629200728/https://www.espn.com/soccer/manchester-united/story/4365318/woodward-out-as-manchester-united-executive-vice-chairman|url-status=live}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56960091|title=Man Utd v Liverpool off after protest|website=BBC Sport|date=2 May 2021|access-date=19 January 2022|archive-date=30 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211130031845/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56960091|url-status=live}} That year, the club matched its record for the biggest win in the Premier League. It [[Manchester United F.C. 9–0 Southampton F.C.|won 9–0]] against Southampton on 2 February 2021.{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55806211|title=Man Utd beat nine-man Southampton 9-0|website=BBC Sport|date=2 February 2021|access-date=19 January 2022|archive-date=15 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210815214453/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55806211|url-status=live}} It lost the [[2021 UEFA Europa League final|UEFA Europa League final]] against [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]], on [[Penalty shoot-out|penalties]]. This was the fourth year without winning a trophy.{{cite news |first=Charlotte |last=Duncker |url=https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/solskjaer-shown-up-familiar-failings-extend-man-utd-trophy/tam5tdvdhrln17nc9z7vw7vwt |title=Solskjaer shown up as familiar failings extend Man Utd's trophy drought |website=goal.com |date=27 May 2021 |access-date=19 January 2022 |archive-date=28 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210628190009/https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/solskjaer-shown-up-familiar-failings-extend-man-utd-trophy/tam5tdvdhrln17nc9z7vw7vwt |url-status=live }} On 20 November 2021, Solskjær left the club.{{cite news |title=Club statement on Ole Gunnar Solskjær |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-statement-on-ole-gunnar-solskjaer |work=Manchester United |date=21 November 2021 |access-date=21 November 2021 |archive-date=15 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220615173120/https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-statement-on-ole-gunnar-solskjaer |url-status=live }} Former midfielder [[Michael Carrick]] became the temporary manager for three games. After this, [[Ralf Rangnick]] became the temporary manager until the end of that season.{{cite news |title=Manchester United appoint Ralf Rangnick as interim manager |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/59439956 |website=BBC Sport |date=29 November 2021 |access-date=19 January 2022 |archive-date=6 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220106192231/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/59439956 |url-status=live }} On 21 April 2022, [[Erik ten Hag]] became the manager from the end of the 2021–22 season. He signed a contract until June 2025 with the option of one more year.{{cite web|url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/erik-ten-hag-appointed-as-man-utd-manager-official-statement|title=Manchester United appoints Erik Ten Hag as Manager|website=manutd.com|date=21 April 2022|access-date=21 April 2022|archive-date=31 May 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220531040020/https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/erik-ten-hag-appointed-as-man-utd-manager-official-statement|url-status=live}} Manchester United won 2–0 in the [[2022–23 EFL Cup|2022–23 EFL Cup final]] against [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]].{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Manchester United 2–0 Newcastle United: Erik ten Hag's side win Carabao Cup for first trophy since 2017 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64693810 |website=BBC Sport |date=26 February 2023 |access-date=27 February 2023 |archive-date=25 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230225230713/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64693810 |url-status=live }} In 2023–2024, Manchester United had a difficult season. The club only finished 8th in the Premier League. This was its lowest finish in the League since 1989–1990.{{Cite web|title=Man Utd end worst Premier League campaign with win|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c4n1nrd4yzpt|access-date=2024-05-25|website=BBC Sport|language=en-GB}} However, the club won its 13th FA Cup against rivals Manchester City, at [[Wembley Stadium|Wembley]] on 25 May 2024.{{Cite news|last=Hytner|first=David|date=2024-05-25|title=Manchester United win FA Cup after Garnacho and Mainoo stun City|language=en-GB|work=The Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/article/2024/may/25/manchester-city-manchester-united-fa-cup-final-match-report|access-date=2024-05-25|issn=0029-7712}} The final finished 2–1 to United. [[Alejandro Garnacho]] and [[Kobbie Mainoo]] both scored in the first half. [[Jeremy Doku]] scored late in the second half for Man City.{{Cite web|title=FA Cup Final 2024 LIVE: Watch Man City vs Man Utd stream plus score, line-ups, commentary & latest updates from Wembley|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c2jj8k5vym5t|access-date=2024-05-25|website=BBC Sport|language=en-GB}} This was Ten Hag's second trophy in two seasons. The following season, Manchester United had their worst start ever in the Premier League. On 28 October 2024, Erik ten Hag was sacked after losing to West Ham United, leaving the club in 14th place. Assistant coach and former United player [[Ruud van Nistelrooy]] became the temporary manager for four games. On 11 November 2024, [[Sporting CP]] manager Ruben Amorim would become the next and most recent permanent manager.{{Cite web|date=1 November 2024|title=United appoint Amorim as new head coach|url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-appoint-ruben-amorim-as-new-head-coach}} == Crest and colours == The club [[Logo|crest]] comes from the [[Manchester City Council#Coat of arms|Manchester City Council coat of arms]]. However, on the current crest only the [[ship]] in full [[sail]] is still there.Barnes et al. (2001), p. 49. The [[devil]] comes from the club's [[nickname]] "The Red Devils". Club [[Event program|programmes]] and [[Scarf|scarves]] in the 1960s had a devil on them. It became part of the club crest in 1970. The club added the crest to the front of the shirt in 1971. Newton Heath's uniform in 1879 has been [[Document|documented]] as 'white with blue cord'.{{cite book|title=The Sportsman's Year-Book for 1880|last=Angus|first=J. Keith|publisher=Cassell, Petter, Galpin & Co.|year=1879|page=182}} This was four years before the club played its first match in a competition. A 1892 photograph of the Newton Heath team seems to show the players wearing red-and-white [[Quarter|quartered]] shirts and [[navy blue]] [[Knickerbockers (clothing)|knickerbockers]].Barnes et al. (2001), p. 48. Between 1894 and 1896, the players wore green and gold shirts. In 1896, these changed to white shirts. They were worn with navy blue [[shorts]]. When the club name changed in 1902, the club changed to red shirts, white shorts and black socks. This became the normal Manchester United home kit (the shirt, shorts and socks). The kit did not change very much until 1922. The club then used white shirts with a dark red "V" around the neck. This was similar to the shirt worn in the [[1909 FA Cup Final]]. This stayed as part of the home kits until 1927. For a period in 1934, the cherry (red) and white hooped (with large [[horizontal]] [[Stripe|stripes]]) change shirt (used when the home shirt was too similar to the other team's) became the home shirt. The season after, the players used the red shirt after the club finished 20th in the Second Division and the hooped shirt became the change shirt again. The club used white socks instead of black from 1959 to 1965. They then used red socks until 1971. They sometimes used white. In 1971, the club used black socks again. The players sometimes still wear black shorts and white socks with the home shirt. This is most often in away games, if the other team's colours are too similar. Starting in 1997–98, United usually used white socks for European games. These matches are usually played during the week in the evening. The white socks help players see the other players in their teams more easily.{{cite news|last=Ogden|first=Mark|date=26 August 2011|title=Sir Alex Ferguson's ability to play the generation game is vital to Manchester United's phenomenal success|website=[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]]|publisher=[[Telegraph Media Group]]|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/manchester-united/8725483/Sir-Alex-Fergusons-ability-to-play-the-generation-game-is-vital-to-Manchester-Uniteds-phenomenal-success.html|accessdate=12 May 2017}} For 2018–19, black shorts and red socks became the main choice for the home kit.{{cite news|date=17 July 2018|title=Adidas launches new United home kit for 2018/19|website=ManUtd.com|publisher=Manchester United|url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/adidas-launches-new-manchester-united-home-kit-for-2018-19-season|accessdate=17 July 2018}} As of 2020, the home kit is a red shirt with the [[trademark]] [[Adidas]] [[three stripes]] in red on the [[Shoulder|shoulders]], white shorts and black socks.{{cite news|date=16 May 2019|title=Revealed: New Man Utd home kit for 2019/20|website=ManUtd.com|publisher=Manchester United|url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/adidas-and-man-utd-launch-new-home-kit-for-2019-20-season|accessdate=17 May 2019}} The Manchester United away kit has often been a white shirt, black shorts and white socks. However, this was not always the away kit. The players sometimes used an all-black kit with blue and gold [[Sewing|trimmings]] between 1993 and 1995. They wore [[navy blue]] shirts with silver horizontal [[Pin stripes|pinstripes]] during the 1999–2000 season.Devlin (2005), p. 157. The 2011–12 away kit had a royal blue chest and sleeves with hoops made of small dark navy blue and black stripes, with black shorts and blue socks.{{cite news|date=15 July 2011|title=Reds unveil new away kit|website=ManUtd.com|publisher=Manchester United|url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Club-News/2011/Jul/manchester-united-unveil-new-away-kit.aspx|accessdate=16 July 2011}} In the 1995–96 season there was an all-[[Gray|grey]] away kit. The team only used it for five games. The last time United used it was against Southampton. Alex Ferguson told the team to change into the third kit at [[half-time]]. The players said it was difficult to see the other players in their team because the colours were similar to the [[Audience|crowd]]. United never won a competitive game in that kit.{{cite news|last=Sharpe|first=Lee|author-link=Lee Sharpe|date=15 April 2006|title=13.04.96 Manchester United's grey day at The Dell|work=The Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2006/apr/15/sport.comment2|accessdate=21 January 2012}} In 2001, to [[Celebration|celebrate]] 100 years as "Manchester United", the club made a [[wikt:reversible|reversible]] white and gold away kit. The real match day shirts (the shirts the players used) were not reversible.Devlin (2005), p. 158. The club's third kit is often all-blue. This was most recently true during the 2014–15 season.{{cite news|date=29 July 2014|title=United reveal blue third kit for 2014/15 season|website=ManUtd.com|publisher=Manchester United|url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Football-News/2014/Jul/New-Manchester-United-third-kit-press-release.aspx|accessdate=30 July 2014}} The players also wore a green-and-gold halved (half green, half gold) shirt between 1992 and 1994. They used a blue-and-white striped shirt during the 1994–95 and 1995–96 seasons and once in 1996–97. They wore an all-black kit during the 1998–99 season when they won the Treble. They used a white shirt with black-and-red horizontal pinstripes between 2003–04 and 2005–06.Devlin (2005), pp. 154–159. From 2006–07 to 2013–14, the third kit was the away kit of the season before. However, they used the new club shirt sponsor in 2006–07 and 2010–11. The only time they did not do this was in 2008–09. They used an all-blue kit to mark the 40th [[anniversary]] of the [[1967–68 European Cup]] win.{{cite news|date=28 August 2008|title=New blue kit for 08/09|website=ManUtd.com|publisher=Manchester
