'''2004''' ([[Roman numerals|MMIV]]) was a [[leap year starting on Thursday]] in the [[Gregorian calendar]].

== Events ==
===January===
*[[January 1]] - [[Joseph Deiss|Deiss]] becomes [[President of the Confederation (Switzerland)|President of the Confederation]] in [[Switzerland]].
*[[January 2]] - Several [[British Airways]] flights from [[London Heathrow Airport]] to [[Washington D.C.]] and [[Riyadh]], [[Saudi Arabia]] are cancelled due to security fears.
*[[January 3]] - [[Flash Airlines Flight 604]] crashes into the [[Red Sea]] off the coast of [[Egypt]]. All 148 aboard are killed.
*[[January 3]] - [[NASA]]'s MER-A (''Spirit'') lands on [[Mars (planet)|Mars]].
*[[January 3]] - [[Tony Blair]] goes to [[Basra]], [[Iraq]] and talks to the [[British people|British]] soldiers there.  Very few people are told before he comes.
*[[January 4]] - Dr. [[Mikhail Saakashvili]] wins presidential elections in the [[Republic of Georgia]].
*  January 4   - A [[NASA]] rover lands on [[Mars (planet)|Mars]] and starts sending back photos of Mars.
*[[January 5]] - [[Britney Spears]]'s marriage to childhood sweetheart [[Jason Allen Alexander]] is annulled (declared invalid) by a [[Las Vegas]] court after a surprise 55-hour marriage.
* January 5    -  [[China]] confirms that a sick man in southern China has the [[SARS]] [[virus]].
*[[January 6]] - An official look into the death of [[Diana, Princess of Wales]] begins in [[London]].  It is held by Michael Burgess, the [[coroner]] of [[Elizabeth II|The Queen]]'s household.
*[[January 12]] - More than 100,000 people come together in [[Tel Aviv]] against [[Prime Minister of Israel|Prime Minister]] [[Ariel Sharon]]'s plan to withdraw from parts of [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]] and the [[West Bank]].
*[[January 13]] - An Uzbekistan Airways plane crashes in [[Uzbekistan]]'s capital of [[Tashkent]]. 37 are killed.
*[[January 14]] - The shock site [[Goatse.cx]] is placed on registry lock for violating the AUP.
*[[January 15]] - The [[South Korea]]n Foreign Minister, Yoon Young-kwan [[Resignation|resign]]s after he says he supports [[United States|American]] policy towards [[North Korea]].
*[[January 20]] - [[India]] signs a $1.5 billion deal with [[Russia]] to buy the 45,000 tonne [[aircraft carrier]] ''Admiral Gorshkov'' along with 28 MiG-29k [[fighter plane]]s.
*[[January 22]] - The [[European Union]] bans the [[import]] of [[poultry]] from [[Thailand]], as [[bird flu]] spreads throughout [[Southeast Asia]].
*[[January 24]] - [[NASA]]'s MER-B (''Opportunity'') lands on [[Mars (planet)|Mars]].
*[[January 28]] - The findings of the Hutton Inquiry are published in [[London]]. The [[British Government]] is found not to have falsified information in the "sexed up dossier". The report criticises the [[BBC]]'s role in the death of [[David Kelly]], a weapons expert on [[Iraq]].
*[[January 28]] - At a hearing of the Commission on Terrorist Attacks Upon the United States, it is revealed that the [[September 11, 2001 attacks|September 11, 2001]] terrorists used [[mace (spray)|mace]] (a brand of [[tear gas]]) or [[pepper spray]] to overpower the flight crew of [[American Airlines Flight 11]].
*[[January 31]] - [[Mystery Science Theatre 3000]] ends its run on the [[Sci-Fi Channel]].

===February===
*[[February 1]] - A [[Hajj]] [[stampede]] in Mina, [[Saudi Arabia]] kills 251 [[Pilgrimage|pilgrim]]s.
*[[February 2]] - An [[apartment building]] falls apart in [[Konya]], [[Turkey]], killing 92.
*[[February 3]] - The [[Central Intelligence Agency|CIA]] admits that there was no immediate threat from [[weapons of mass destruction]] before the [[2003 invasion of Iraq]].
*[[February 4]] - [[Facebook]] is launched.
*[[February 6]] - A [[suicide bomber]] kills 41 people on a [[Rapid transit|subway]] train in [[Moscow]].
*[[February 7]] - His Royal Highness [[Charles, Prince of Wales]] begins a tour of the [[Middle East]], visiting troops in [[Iraq]], the [[Iran]]ian earthquake zone at [[Bam]] and [[Saudi Arabia]].
*[[February 10]] - At least 50 people are killed in a [[car bomb]] attack at a center for hiring police officers south of [[Baghdad]].
*[[February 10]] - The [[French National Assembly]] votes to pass a law [[ban]]ning religious items and clothing from schools.
*[[February 11]] - Up to 47 people are killed in a [[car bomb]] attack on an army recruiting center in [[Baghdad]].
*[[February 12]] - Same sex marriage in the United States: The [[San Francisco, California|City and County of San Francisco]] begins giving out marriage licenses to homosexual couples as an act of [[civil disobedience]].
*[[February 13]] - Scientists in [[South Korea]] announce the [[cloning]] of 30 human [[embryo]]s.
*[[February 17]] - [[90482 Orcus]] is discovered (found)
*[[February 18]] - A train carrying gas, fertiliser and sulphur [[Derailment|derail]]s and explodes in [[Iran]], killing 320 people.
*[[February 20]] - [[Iran Majlis election, 2004|Iranian parliament election]] is held.  Many [[reformist]] candidates are not allowed to run, resulting in a win by [[conservatism|conservatives]].
*[[February 22]] - A [[suicide bomber]] kills eight bus passengers in [[Jerusalem]].
*[[February 22]] - [[Rebellion|Rebels]] capture [[Haiti]]'s second-largest city, [[Cap-Haïtien]].
*[[February 24]] - An [[earthquake]] in [[Morocco]] kills 571 people.
*[[February 26]] - Former British [[cabinet minister]], Clare Short reveals that [[MI6|British Intelligence]] [[Telephone tapping|bugged]] the phone calls of [[United Nations]] officials, including [[Kofi Annan]].
*[[February 26]] - The [[United States]] lifts a ban on travel to [[Libya]], ending travel restrictions that had lasted for 23 years.
*[[February 29]] - 2004 Haiti Rebellion: [[Jean-Bertrand Aristide]] resigns as [[president of Haiti]]. The chief justice of the Haitian Supreme Court, [[Boniface Alexandre]], is sworn in as interim (short-term) president. Aristide later says he was made to resign, and that he was taken from the country by [[United States|American]] soldiers.

===March===
*[[March 1]] - [[Prime Minister of the Palestinian National Authority|Prime Minister]] Ahmed Qurie blasted ongoing [[Israel]]i extrajudicial [[execution]]s of [[Palestinian]] [[activist]]s, which claimed two more lives on Sunday, and blamed Israel for the weekend of violence, whilst accusing his Israeli counterpart’s government of trying "to kill any possibility for (achieving a) mutual [[Ceasefire|cease-fire]]".<ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-02-29|title=Israel told to halt barrier work|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/middle_east/3520115.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref>
*[[March 1]] - [[Jean-Bertrand Aristide]] claims that his resignation as [[President of Haiti]] was forced and that he was kidnapped by American forces and forced to leave the country against his will. [[United States Vice President]] [[Dick Cheney]] rejects the accusation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Democracy Now! | website=[[Democracy Now!]] |url=http://www.democracynow.org/index.pl?issue=20040301 |access-date=2013-07-09 |archive-date=2006-07-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060721144302/http://www.democracynow.org/index.pl?issue=20040301 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=CNN.com - Rebel leader threatens Haiti PM - Mar. 3, 2004|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2004/WORLD/americas/03/02/haiti.rebels/|access-date=2022-05-08|website=edition.cnn.com|archive-date=2022-03-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220321182157/http://edition.cnn.com/2004/WORLD/americas/03/02/haiti.rebels/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
*[[March 1]] - [[President of Russia]] [[Vladimir Putin]] names [[Mikhail Fradkov]] as his new [[Prime Minister of Russia|prime minister]].<ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-01|title=Putin names new prime minister|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/3521591.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref>
*[[March 1]] - Several hundred [[United States]], [[France|French]] and [[Canada|Canadian]] troops are sent to [[Haiti]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2004-03-02|title=Troops start peacekeeping in Haiti|url=https://www.theage.com.au/national/troops-start-peacekeeping-in-haiti-20040302-gdigkd.html|access-date=2022-05-08|website=The Age|language=en}}</ref>
*[[March 2]] -  The [[Palestinian Authority]]'s prisoners' affairs ministry states in its monthly statistical report that the number of Palestinian prisoners has risen to around 7,500. Of those 336 are children, 75 are female, and 943 are in need of medical treatment. Of the 166 prisoners who died, 41% died as a result of medical negligence, while 18% died as a result of [[torture]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Same day loans UK|url=https://www.pales.co.uk/same-day-loans/same-day-loans-uk/|access-date=2022-05-08|website=Pales Tine Payday Loans Info|language=en-GB|archive-date=2022-05-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220522231857/https://www.pales.co.uk/same-day-loans/same-day-loans-uk/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
*[[March 2]] -  [[Israel]]'s Central Bureau of Statistics reports 1,850 new housing units in the Jewish settlements Israel built in the [[West Bank]] and [[Gaza Strip]] in 2003, up by 35 percent from the previous year.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-02|title=Israeli settlement building grows|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/middle_east/3526791.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref>
*[[March 2]] -  [[John Kerry]] wins the [[Super Tuesday]] [[Primary election|primaries]] in [[California]], [[Connecticut]], [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]], [[Maryland]], [[Massachusetts]], [[New York (state)|New York]], [[Ohio]], and [[Rhode Island]], and the [[caucus]] in [[Minnesota]], effectively winning the nomination. [[Howard Dean]] wins in his home state of [[Vermont]] even though he is no longer actively campaigning. [[John Edwards]] is reported to be withdrawing from the race three hours before polls close in California and just as the caucuses begin in Minnesota.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.newsobserver.com/24hour/election/story/1173348p-8116744c.html |title=NC News & Observer |access-date=2013-07-09 |archive-date=2004-08-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040808093402/http://www.newsobserver.com/24hour/election/story/1173348p-8116744c.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*[[March 2]] - Jason West, mayor of [[New Paltz, New York|New Paltz]], [[New York (state)|New York]] is charged with 19 criminal counts of performing marriages without a license. If convicted, he faces up to a $500 fine and a year in jail on each count.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Newsday {{!}} Long Island's & NYC's News Source|url=https://www.newsday.com/|access-date=2022-05-08|website=Newsday}}</ref>
*[[March 2]] - [[Exploration of Mars]]: [[NASA]] announces that [[Mars (planet)|Mars]] rover ''Opportunity'' landed in an area where "liquid water once drenched the surface".<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=%2Fnews%2Farchive%2F2004%2F03%2F02%2Fstate1405EST0076.DTL |title=SF Chronicle |access-date=2021-10-05 |archive-date=2005-12-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051202124521/http://sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=%2Fnews%2Farchive%2F2004%2F03%2F02%2Fstate1405EST0076.DTL |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*[[March 2]] - [[Bernard Ebbers]], ex-[[CEO]] of Worldcom, is [[indicted]] on three counts of [[conspiracy]] for his alleged role in that company's $11 billion accounting scandal in [[2002]].  Worldcom's CFO Scott Sullivan pleads guilty and is expected to cooperate with prosecutors against Ebbers.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ebbers charged in WorldCom case, Sullivan pleads guilty - Mar. 2, 2004|url=https://money.cnn.com/2004/03/02/technology/ebbers/index.htm?CNN=yes|access-date=2022-05-08|website=money.cnn.com|archive-date=2022-05-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220508065648/https://money.cnn.com/2004/03/02/technology/ebbers/index.htm?CNN=yes|url-status=dead}}</ref>
*[[March 2]] - Multiple explosions hit [[Shiite]] shrines in [[Baghdad]] and [[Karbala]] on the [[Shia]] festival of [[Ashura]]. Over 180 people are reported killed. A three-day long period of national [[mourning]] is announced.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-02|title=Iraq Shias massacred on holy day|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/middle_east/3524589.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref>
*[[March 2]] - [[Iraq]] gets a [[Bill of Rights]], including guarantees of [[freedom of religion]] and [[freedom of the press|press]], in the form of the Law of Administering the Iraqi State for the Transitional Period.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Iraqi council OKs bill of rights|url=https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2004/mar/2/20040302-123023-2851r/|access-date=2022-05-08|website=The Washington Times|date=2 March 2004 |language=en-US}}</ref>
*[[March 2]] - The U.S. declares its 2,000-man force to have leadership over all foreign military forces in [[Haiti]]. [[George W. Bush|President Bush]] chose not to wait for the [[UN Security Council]] but, instead, to intervene immediately to "restore order" in the [[western hemisphere]]'s poorest country.<ref>{{Cite web|title=U.S. to send 'small' operation to Haiti|url=https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2004/mar/2/20040302-124237-3685r/|access-date=2022-05-08|website=The Washington Times|date=2 March 2004 |language=en-US}}</ref>
*[[March 2]] - The [[European Union]] imposes additional 5% [[tariff]]s on a wide range of goods imported from the [[United States]], such as [[honey]], [[paper]], and [[nuclear reactor]]s. The tariffs were sanctioned by the [[World Trade Organization]] in [[2002]] as [[punishment|punitive measures]] after a ruling declaring that United States [[tax]] law unfairly favors U.S.-based companies.<ref>{{Cite news|title=BBC NEWS {{!}} Business {{!}} EU opens new front in trade war|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/business/3521731.stm|access-date=2022-05-08|website=news.bbc.co.uk|date=March 2004 }}</ref>
*[[March 2]] - The [[European Space Agency]]'s Rosetta space probe is successfully launched aboard an [[Ariane 5]] rocket on a mission to investigate the [[comet]] 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-02|title=Rosetta probe heads for comet|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/science/nature/3522535.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref>
*[[March 3]] -  At the [[Walt Disney Company]]'s Annual General Meeting, about 43% of Walt Disney [[stockholder]]s, including several prominent [[pension]] funds, vote to oppose the re-election of [[chairman]] and [[Chief executive officer|CEO]] [[Michael Eisner]]. The [[board of directors]] replaces him as chairman with [[George J. Mitchell]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Eisner losers Disney chairman job, stays as CEO - Mar. 4, 2004|url=https://money.cnn.com/2004/03/03/news/companies/disney/index.htm?=|access-date=2022-05-08|website=money.cnn.com|archive-date=2022-05-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220508065646/https://money.cnn.com/2004/03/03/news/companies/disney/index.htm?=|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Holson|first=Laura M.|date=2004-03-04|title=Defied in Vote, Disney Leader Loses One Post|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/03/04/business/defied-in-vote-disney-leader-loses-one-post.html|access-date=2022-05-08|issn=0362-4331}}</ref>
*[[March 3]] - [[Research]]ers at [[Harvard University]] announce that they will give scientists free access to 17 human [[embryo]]nic [[stem cell]] lines created without U.S. federal funding.  This move is expected to help stem cell research in the face of federal funding restrictions announced in [[2001]] by the [[George W. Bush|Bush administration]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Harvard gives free access to new stem cell lines - Mar. 3, 2004|url=http://www.cnn.com/2004/HEALTH/03/03/harvard.stemcells.ap/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080607112231/http://www.cnn.com/2004/HEALTH/03/03/harvard.stemcells.ap/index.html|archive-date=2008-06-07|access-date=2022-05-08|website=CNN}}</ref>
*[[March 3]] - A new government of [[Serbia]], headed by Vojislav Kostunica, is approved by [[parliament]].<ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-02|title=Kostunica introduces new cabinet|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/3526783.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref>
*[[March 3]] - [[March 3]] -  [[Israel]]i aircraft destroy a car in the [[Gaza strip]] with [[missile]] fire, killing three people acknowledged by Palestinian officials as members of the [[militant group]] [[Hamas]].<ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-03|title=Israel strike kills three in Gaza|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/middle_east/3529439.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref>
*[[March 3]] - [[March 3]] -  A group of [[Israel]]is join a court challenge against the [[Israeli West Bank barrier]] out of concern it could turn their good Palestinian neighbors into deadly enemies.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2005-04-08|title=Top News Article|website=[[Reuters]] |url=http://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml?type=topNews&storyID=4486274|access-date=2022-05-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050408171624/http://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml?type=topNews&storyID=4486274 |archive-date=2005-04-08 }}</ref>
*[[March 3]] -  New claims of bubble fusion are made, claiming that the results of previous experiments have been replicated under more stringent experimental conditions.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.rpi.edu/web/News/press_releases/2004/lahey.htm |title=RPI press release |access-date=2013-07-09 |archive-date=2005-04-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050403143057/http://www.rpi.edu/web/News/press_releases/2004/lahey.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Experts Say New Desktop Fusion Claims Seem More Credible|url=http://www.rpi.edu/web/News/nytlahey3.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050404150628/http://www.rpi.edu/web/News/nytlahey3.html|archive-date=2005-04-04|access-date=2013-07-09}}</ref>
*[[March 4]] - Bomb blasts in [[Iraq]] threaten to de-stabilise the country.
*[[March 4]] -  The [[guilt (law)|guilty]] [[verdict]] for [[Moroccan]] [[al-Qaeda]] suspect Mounir el Motassadeq's involvement in the [[September 11, 2001 attacks]] is overturned by the [[Germany|German]] appeals court, which orders a retrial.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Guilty verdict overturned in al-Qaeda suspect's case|website=[[The Globe and Mail]] |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/servlet/ArticleNews/TPStory/LAC/20040305/GERMANY05/TPInternational/Americas|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040813161650/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/servlet/ArticleNews/TPStory/LAC/20040305/GERMANY05/TPInternational/Americas|archive-date=2004-08-13|access-date=2017-08-21}}</ref>
*[[March 4]] - Three [[United States|American]] [[Muslim]]s accused of using [[paintball]] games to train for a ''[[jihad]]'' holy war are found guilty of [[conspiracy]] charges.<ref>{{Cite web|title='Paintball Terrorists' Convicted of Conspiracy|url=https://www.foxnews.com/printer_friendly_story/0,3566,113310,00.html|access-date=2022-05-08|website=www.foxnews.com}}</ref>
*[[March 4]] - [[People's Republic of China|Chinese]] authorities release Wang Youcai, a day after Rabiya Kadeer's release <ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-04|title=Top Chinese dissident released|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/asia-pacific/3531965.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref>
*[[March 4]] - [[Israel]]i [[tank]]s around 15 armoured vehicles escorted by several [[bulldozer]]s enter the town of [[Rafah]] in the southern [[Gaza Strip]], exchanging gunfire with resistance and later demolishing a four-storey building, claiming "anti-terrorist operations".{{Fact|date=May 2022}}
*[[March 4]] -  The [[Prime Minister of Malaysia]] dissolves the [[Parliament of Malaysia|national parliament]] and all state assemblies except [[Sarawak]]'s, paving the way for the general election to be held within 60 days as dictated by the constitution.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-05|title=Malaysia decides on election date|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/asia-pacific/3531521.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref>
*[[March 5]] - [[CBS]] broadcasts tape recordings of [[Diana, Princess of Wales]] as she describes [[suicide]] attempts while pregnant with [[Prince William, Duke of Cambridge]].
*[[March 5]] -  The [[National People's Congress]] convenes in [[Beijing]]. [[Premier of the People's Republic of China|Premier]] [[Wen Jiabao]] makes his first state address, saying that "solving the problems of [[agriculture]], villages and farmers is one of the most crucial parts of our entire work".<ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-05|title=China vows help for rural poor|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/asia-pacific/3534833.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref>
*[[March 5]] -  Last minute disagreement delays signing of [[Iraq]]'s interim [[constitution]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Disagreements Delay Signing Of Iraqi Constitution|url=https://www.rferl.org/a/1051788.html|access-date=2022-05-08|website=RadioFreeEurope/RadioLiberty|date=8 April 2008 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Iraq council won't sign new constitution|url=https://usatoday30.usatoday.com/news/world/iraq/2004-03-05-iraq_x.htm|access-date=2022-05-08|website=USATODAY.com}}</ref>
*[[March 5]] -  The [[Russia]]n polar station will be evacuated. Russia launches rescue operation to evacuate 12 of its [[scientist]]s stranded on a [[research station]] which partially sank near the [[North Pole]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Russian polar station will be evacuated|url=http://newsfromrussia.com/main/2004/03/05/52656.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070929121843/http://newsfromrussia.com/main/2004/03/05/52656.html|archive-date=2007-09-29|access-date=2013-07-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-06|title=Russia launches Arctic rescue bid|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/3535383.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref>
*[[March 5]] -  [[Tony Blair]] defends the [[2003 invasion of Iraq|war in Iraq]], stating that "global threat we face in [[UK|Britain]] and round the [[world]] is real and existential and it is the task of [[leadership]] to expose it and fight it, whatever the political cost." <ref>{{Cite web|date=2004-03-05|title=Full text: Tony Blair's speech|url=http://www.theguardian.com/politics/2004/mar/05/iraq.iraq|access-date=2022-05-08|website=the Guardian|language=en}}</ref>
*[[March 5]] -  [[Police]] hold a [[Haifa]] man,  Eliran Golan, and his 54-year-old father in custody on suspicion of involvement in making and planting [[bomb]]s over the last three years. Haifa Magistrate court extends for five days the remand of Yivgeny Grossman. Grossman denies any connection.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Haifa Jew suspected in 9 anti-Arab bombings|url=http://www.haaretz.com/hasen/spages/401407.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040312030505/http://www.haaretz.com/hasen/spages/401407.html|archive-date=2004-03-12|access-date=2013-07-09}}</ref>
*[[March 5]] -  [[Martha Stewart]] is found guilty by a [[jury]] on charges of [[conspiracy]], [[obstruction of justice]], and two counts of making false statements regarding alleged [[insider trading]] in December 2001. She faces up to 20 years in prison, though it is considered unlikely that she would be sentenced to that maximum. Sentencing is set for [[June 17]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Martha Stewart convicted of all counts in stock-trading trial|url=http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=%2Fnews%2Farchive%2F2004%2F03%2F05%2Fnational1508EST0626.DTL|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060301085536/http://www.sfgate.com:80/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=/news/archive/2004/03/05/national1508EST0626.DTL|archive-date=2006-03-01|access-date=2021-10-05}}</ref>
*[[March 5]] -  Nunavut general election, 2004: the new [[legislature]] returns [[Paul Okalik]] to office as [[Premier of Nunavut]], the largest [[List of Canadian provinces and territories|territory]] of [[Canada]].<ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-02-17|title=Incumbents have good night in Nunavut election|language=en-CA|work=The Globe and Mail|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/national/incumbents-have-good-night-in-nunavut-election/article20428123/|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref>
*[[March 5]] -  Key [[Tokyo Metropolis|Tokyo]] stock indexes [[Nikkei 225]] and Topix hit 21-month highs.
*[[March 5]] -  The trial of former [[Prime Minister of Finland]] [[Anneli Jäätteenmäki]] ends. She has been accused of leaking secret foreign ministry documents referring to her predecessor [[Paavo Lipponen]]'s meetings with [[George W. Bush]].<ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-05|title=Trial of former Finnish PM ends|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/3537531.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref>
*[[March 6]] - Tens of thousands [[Demonstration|demonstrate]] in [[Caracas]], [[Venezuela]], against what they see as the government's [[fraud]] committed by the Consejo Nacional Electoral related to the realization of a presidential [[referendum]] in mid-2004.
*[[March 6]] - The [[United States]] puts forth a [[UN Security Council]] resolution seeking to freeze the assets of [[Charles Taylor]], the exiled former [[President of Liberia]]. The U.S. also announces that it is pledging $35 million to help rebuild Liberia's [[armed forces]] and that it supports the cancellation of Liberia's international [[debt]], providing that economic reforms are implemented.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-06|title=US targets Liberia leader's funds|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/africa/3538553.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref>
*[[March 6]] - [[Palestinian]]s are killed and wounded in attack on the main crossing point between the [[Gaza Strip]] and [[Israel]]. [[Hamas]], [[Islamic Jihad]], and the [[al-Aqsa Martyrs Brigades]] claim responsibility.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-06|title=Deadly assault on Gaza crossing|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/middle_east/3538607.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref>
*[[March 6]] - Up to 80,000 people march through the [[Turkey|Turkish]] capital [[Ankara]] against plans to reform the country's [[civil service]]. The marchers fear that the reforms could lead to the civil service becoming politicised or losing its secular status.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-06|title=Mass march against Turkish reform|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/3539881.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref>
*[[March 6]] - The scientists of the [[Russia]]n polar [[research station]] near the [[North Pole]] are evacuated from their shifting and cracking ice floe by two Russian helicopters via Norway's Spitzbergen island.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-06|title=Scientists rescued from ice floe|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/3538937.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref>
*[[March 7]] - The [[New York City]] [[medical examiner]] reveals that a [[corpse|body]] pulled from the [[East River]] is that of actor/writer [[Spalding Gray]], who had been missing since January.<ref>{{Cite news|last1=Dewan|first1=Shaila K.|last2=McKinley|first2=Jesse|date=2004-03-09|title=Body of Spalding Gray Found; Monologuist and Actor Was 62|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/03/09/nyregion/body-of-spalding-gray-found-monologuist-and-actor-was-62.html|access-date=2022-05-08|issn=0362-4331}}</ref>
*March 7 - Greek legislative election, 2004: New Democracy, led by [[Costas Karamanlis]], wins over the Panhellenic Socialist Movement, led by [[George Papandreou]].<ref name="news.bbc.co.uk">{{Cite news|date=2004-03-07|title=Greek conservatives seize power|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/3540163.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref>
*March 7 -  An explosion rocks a [[Moscow]] apartment block. Initial reports from [[police]] suggest that the explosion was caused by a [[bomb]], in spite of increased security before the presidential election on [[March 14]]. Later reports state that the explosion was due to a [[natural gas|gas]] leak.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-07|title='Gas blast' hits flats in Moscow|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/3540077.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref>
*March 7 - The [[White House]] reports that all of [[Libya]]'s remaining [[weapons of mass destruction|nuclear weapons-related equipment]] has been sent to the [[United States]].<ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-07|title=Libya ships out last WMD parts|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/africa/3539799.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref>
*March 7 - [[Palestinian Authority|Palestinian]] sources say that 14 people died after an [[Israel]]i raid into the refugee camps of al-Bureij and Nusseirat. Israeli sources say it was a "pinpoint" operation against the "terrorist infrastructure".<ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-07|title=Israeli incursion leaves 14 dead|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/middle_east/3540179.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref>
*March 7 - The 2004 [[Formula One]] championship gets under way with the [[Australian Grand Prix]] in [[Melbourne]]. [[Michael Schumacher]] wins.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-07|title=Ferrari dominate first race|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/motorsport/formula_one/3539193.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref>
*March 7 - In [[Sweden]] some 15,500 skiers compete in the 80th installment of [[Vasaloppet]], the oldest and longest [[cross-country skiing|cross-country ski race]] in the world. [[Norway|Norwegian]] Anders Aukland wins.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Aukland becomes first Norwegian winner in 33 years|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2004/more/03/07/bc.eu.spt.ski.cross.vasaloppet.ap/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040830094246/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2004/more/03/07/bc.eu.spt.ski.cross.vasaloppet.ap/index.html|archive-date=2004-08-30|access-date=2013-07-09}}</ref>
*March 7 - In [[Austria]] there are elections in the states of Salzburg and Carinthia. In Salzburg, the [[SPÖ]] earns a majority for the first time. In Carinthia, the election is an unexpected success for [[Jörg Haider]] [[FPÖ]].
*March 7 - It is announced that [[Peter Maxwell Davies]] is to be the United Kingdom's next [[Master of the Queen's Music]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Connie Fisher|date=2004-03-07|title=New Master of The Queen's Music|url=https://www.royal.uk/new-master-queens-music|access-date=2022-05-08|website=The Royal Family|language=en}}</ref>
*March 7 - The headquarters of the United States-led coalition in [[Baghdad]] come under rocket attack from Iraqi guerillas, the day before the new [[Iraq]]i temporary constitution is due to be signed.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-07|title=Explosions rock centre of Baghdad|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/middle_east/3541321.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref>
*[[March 8]] -  Dr. Jiang Yanyong, who exposed the [[SARS]] coverup in the [[People's Republic of China]], sends a letter to the [[National People's Congress]] calling the forceful suppression of the [[Tiananmen Square protests of 1989]] a "mistake." <ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-08|title=China doctor calls 1989 'mistake'|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/asia-pacific/3542049.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref>
*[[March 8]] -  [[Iraq]]'s governing council unanimously approves the country's new [[constitution]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Governing Council Lays|url=https://govinfo.library.unt.edu/cpa-iraq/transcripts/20040308_signing_transcript.html|access-date=2022-05-08|website=govinfo.library.unt.edu}}</ref>
*[[March 8]] -  On [[International Women's Day]], [[Afghanistan|Afghan]] President [[Hamid Karzai]] encourages men to allow their female relatives to [[vote]] in the upcoming election, but also suggests that they control those votes.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Foreign operations, export financing, and related programs appropriations for fiscal year 2005 : hearings before a subcommittee of the Committee on Appropriations, United States Senate, One Hundred Eighth Congress, second session, on H.R. 4818/S. 2812, an act making appropriations for foreign operations, export financing, and related programs for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2005, and for other purposes.|date=2005|isbn=9780160744624|location=Washington|pages=101|oclc=62383051}}</ref>
*[[March 9]] - A restaurant in [[Istanbul]], [[Turkey]] is attacked by two [[Islamic]] suicide bombers killing one, injuring five.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Freemasons, targeted by bombing, viewed with suspicion in Turkey|url=http://www.channelnewsasia.com/stories/afp_world/view/74815/1/.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051205181735/http://www.channelnewsasia.com/stories/afp_world/view/74815/1/.html|archive-date=2005-12-05|access-date=2013-07-09}}</ref>
*[[March 9]] - New [[hubble Space Telescope]] images show deepest view of the universe yet.<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2004/03/09/science/space/09CND-HUBB.html?ex=1079499600&en=cfad33ff91ec4f91&ei=5062&partner=GOOGLE NYT]</ref>
*[[March 9]] - [[John Allen Muhammad]] is sentenced to death by a [[Virginia]] judge because he was part of the [[Beltway sniper attacks]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sniper Muhammad sentenced to death|url=http://www.cnn.com/2004/LAW/03/09/sniper/|access-date=2022-05-08|website=www.cnn.com}}</ref>
*[[March 9]] - A genetically modified crop, [[Bayer]]'s Chardon LL [[maize]], is approved for growing in [[England]] for animal feed from 2005 until October 2006. The Scottish Executive also approves the move, but asks Scottish farmers to hold off. MPs and farmers protest in anger as the science is questioned. The [[National Assembly for Wales|Welsh National Assembly]]'s Environment Minister announces he is still opposed to approving the crop.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-09|title=UK's tentative go-ahead for GMs|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/science/nature/3546347.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-09|title=Executive backs UK GM crop move|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/scotland/3545825.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-09|title=Wales refuses GM agreement|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/wales/3545447.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Fury over GM crops|url=http://www.thisislondon.co.uk/news/articles/9539377?source=Evening%20Standard|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051129042025/http://www.thisislondon.co.uk/news/articles/9539377?source=Evening%20Standard|archive-date=2005-11-29|access-date=2013-07-09}}</ref>
*[[March 9]] - [[Pakistan]] announces a successful first flight test of its Hatf VI / Shaheen II long-range [[nuclear weapon|nuclear]]-capable [[ballistic missile]]. The missile has a range of 2,000 km 1,250 mi and can carry a payload of 1,000 kg 2,200 lb.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-09|title=Pakistan tests long-range missile|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/south_asia/3545775.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Pakistan tests long-range missile|url=http://us.cnn.com/2004/WORLD/asiapcf/03/09/pakistan.missile/index.html|access-date=2022-05-08|website=us.cnn.com|archive-date=2022-03-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220321182225/http://us.cnn.com/2004/WORLD/asiapcf/03/09/pakistan.missile/index.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>
*[[March 9]] -  Five of the nine Britons held by American authorities at [[Guantanamo Bay]] under suspicion of having links to terrorist organisations are returned to Britain. They are to be questioned by British anti-terrorism police on arrival.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Gitmo men arrested upon UK return|website=[[CNN]] |url=http://www.cnn.com/2004/WORLD/europe/03/09/gitmo.uk/|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081218043212/http://www.cnn.com/2004/WORLD/europe/03/09/gitmo.uk/|archive-date=2008-12-18|access-date=2013-07-09}}</ref>
*[[March 9]] - The [[FBI]] arrests William Cottrell, a [[Caltech]] student and alleged member of the Earth Liberation Front, in connection with last summer's spate of [[arson]] attacks at a car dealerships which destroyed or damaged over one hundred vehicles, including many [[Hummer]] H2 luxury [[SUV]]s.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Charges In Torching Of 125 SUVs|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/charges-in-torching-of-125-suvs/|access-date=2022-05-08|website=www.cbsnews.com|language=en-US}}</ref>
*[[March 10]] - Five British men released from detention at Camp Delta, [[Guantanamo Bay]] land at RAF Brize Norton. Four are immediately arrested by the [[Metropolitan Police]] and taken to Paddington Green high security police station in Central [[London]] for questioning.
*[[March 10]] - Lee Boyd Malvo is sentenced to life in prison without parole by a [[Virginia]] judge for his role in the Beltway Sniper Attacks.<ref>{{Cite web|title=CNN.com - Sniper Malvo sentenced to life without parole - Mar 11, 2004|url=http://www.cnn.com/2004/LAW/03/10/sniper.malvo/|access-date=2022-05-08|website=www.cnn.com}}</ref>
*[[March 11]] - The Spirit rover takes first [[picture]] of [[Earth]] ever made from the surface of another [[planet]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mars Rovers See Earth, Moons and Stars|website=[[Space.com]] |url=http://www.space.com/scienceastronomy/mars_earth_040311.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101224210135/http://www.space.com/scienceastronomy/mars_earth_040311.html|archive-date=2010-12-24|access-date=2013-07-09}}</ref>
*[[March 11]] - [[March 11, 2004 Madrid attacks]]: 10 bombs on [[Madrid]] [[commuter train]]s kill at least 180 people and hurt more than 1400.  This is the most people ever hurt in any bombing in [[Europe]] since the crash of [[Pan Am Flight 103]] in [[Lockerbie]].<ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-11|title=Scores die in Madrid bomb carnage|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/3500452.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Al menos 192 muertos y más de 1.400 heridos en una cadena de atentados en trenes de cercanías en Madrid|url=http://www.lavanguardia.es/web/20040311/51152856332.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040314212011/http://www.lavanguardia.es/web/20040311/51152856332.html|archive-date=2004-03-14|access-date=2013-07-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=CNN.com - Police search for Madrid bombers - Mar 12, 2004|url=http://www.cnn.com/2004/WORLD/europe/03/11/spain.blasts/index.html|access-date=2022-05-08|website=www.cnn.com}}</ref>
*[[March 11]] - Four [[UK|British]] prisoners who had been arrested on their return from [[Guantanamo Bay]] are released without charge. A fifth was not arrested on arrival. A further four remain in the [[Cuba]]n camp. British newspapers vie for the rights to their stories, with offers in the range of £300,000. These five people are expected to sue the United States and UK governments.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2004-03-11|title=All detainees returned from Cuba released|url=http://www.theguardian.com/uk/2004/mar/11/september11.guantanamo|access-date=2022-05-08|website=the Guardian|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-11|title='Delight' at release of Guantanamo men|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/3500156.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=2004-03-11|title=What next for Guantanamo five?|language=en-GB|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/3500202.stm|access-date=2022-05-08}}</ref>
*[[March 11]] - [[Same-sex marriage in the United States]]: The California Supreme Court issues an rule ordering [[San Francisco]] officials to stop issuing marriage licenses to same-sex couples. The court said it would hear oral arguments regarding the controversy in May or June. The state says it did not register any of the thousands of recent [[gay marriage]]s.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Court calls off same-sex 'weddings'|url=https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2004/mar/12/20040312-120646-7708r/|access-date=2022-05-08|website=The Washington Times|date=12 March 2004 |language=en-US}}</ref>
*[[March 11]] - [[United Nations|UN]] inspectors find [[nuclear weapon|weapons]]-grade [[uranium]] in [[Iran]]. Iran objects to UN and [[United States]] policy, considering it "unrealistic." <ref>{{Cite web|title=Iran's 'right to enrich' uranium|url=http://www.atimes.com/atimes/Middle_East/FC12Ak02.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121022132115/http://www.atimes.com/atimes/Middle_East/FC12Ak02.html|archive-date=2012-10-22|access-date=2013-07-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Iran's President Threatens Halt In Nuclear Cooperation With UN|url=https://www.rferl.org/a/1051849.html|access-date=2022-05-08|website=RadioFreeEurope/RadioLiberty|date=8 April 2008 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Smith|first=Craig S.|date=2004-03-11|title=Alarm Raised Over Quality Of Uranium Found in Iran|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/03/11/world/alarm-raised-over-quality-of-uranium-found-in-iran.html|access-date=2022-05-08|issn=0362-4331}}</ref>
*[[March 11]] - A [[Maryland]] woman and former [[U.S. Democratic Party|Democrat]]ic congressional aide, Susan Lindauer, is arrested on charges of conspiracy against the [[United States]], acting as an [[Iraq]]i [[Espionage|spy]] before and during last year's invasion.<ref>{{Cite web|title=U.S. woman charged with spying for Iraq|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2004/LAW/03/11/iraq.spy.case.ap/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040405015819/http://edition.cnn.com/2004/LAW/03/11/iraq.spy.case.ap/index.html|archive-date=2004-04-05|access-date=2013-07-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2010-07-22|title=Woman Accused Of Spying For Saddam|url=http://www.thesmokinggun.com/documents/crime/woman-accused-spying-saddam|access-date=2022-05-08|website=The Smoking Gun|language=en}}</ref>
*[[March 11]] - An [[Australian Senate]] report on [[poverty]] is immediately dismissed by [[Prime Minister of Australia|Prime Minister]] [[John Howard]]. The report shows between 2 and 3.5 million [[Australia]]ns, or up to 19 per cent of the population, are living in poverty.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2004-03-12|title=Howard dismisses push for poverty taskforce|url=https://www.theage.com.au/national/howard-dismisses-push-for-poverty-taskforce-20040312-gdxhaw.html|access-date=2022-05-08|website=The Age|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Poverty probe torn by politics|url=http://www.thewest.com.au/20040312/news/general/tw-news-general-home-sto121382.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040416054355/http://www.thewest.com.au/20040312/news/general/tw-news-general-home-sto121382.html|archive-date=2004-04-16|access-date=2013-07-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Official report finds growing gap between Australia's rich and poor|url=http://www.channelnewsasia.com/stories/afp_asiapacific_business/view/74916/1/.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050508153814/http://www.channelnewsasia.com/stories/afp_asiapacific_business/view/74916/1/.html|archive-date=2005-05-08|access-date=2013-07-09}}</ref>
*[[March 12]] - A [[Utah]] woman is charged with [[murder]] when her child is [[stillborn]] because she did not want to have a [[Caesarean section]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.reuters.co.uk/newsPackageArticle.jhtml?type=worldNews&storyID=475091&section=news |title=Reuters |access-date=2013-07-09 |archive-date=2004-08-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040831083311/http://www.reuters.co.uk/newsPackageArticle.jhtml?type=worldNews&storyID=475091&section=news |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?file=%2Fnews%2Farchive%2F2004%2F03%2F12%2Fnational1711EST0684.DTL |title=SF Chronicle |access-date=2021-10-05 |archive-date=2007-08-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070810085038/http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?file=%2Fnews%2Farchive%2F2004%2F03%2F12%2Fnational1711EST0684.DTL |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.thestar.com/NASApp/cs/ContentServer?pagename=thestar%2FLayout%2FArticle_Type1&c=Article&cid=1079133608534&call_pageid=968332188492&col=968705899037 |title=Toronto Star |website=[[Toronto Star]] |access-date=2021-09-26 |archive-date=2011-06-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110606155419/http://www.thestar.com/NASApp/cs/ContentServer?pagename=thestar%2FLayout%2FArticle_Type1&c=Article&cid=1079133608534&call_pageid=968332188492&col=968705899037 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*[[March 12]] -  Millions of people pack rainy streets across [[Spain]] in protest against the recent Madrid bombings.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml?type=worldNews&storyID=4558577&section=news |title=Reuters |website=[[Reuters]] |access-date=2017-08-30 |archive-date=2005-03-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050306101113/http://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml?type=worldNews&storyID=4558577&section=news |url-status=dead }}</ref>

[[Prime Minister of South Korea|Prime Minister]] [[Goh Kun]] will run the country until the Constitutional Court rules on the issue. Roh's supporters dismiss the move as a power play to influence the upcoming April elections. Thousands protest in support of Roh.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml?type=worldNews&storyID=4552698 |title=Reuters |website=[[Reuters]] |access-date=2017-08-30 |archive-date=2005-04-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050408151639/http://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml?type=worldNews&storyID=4552698 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/asia-pacific/3504026.stm BBC]</ref><ref>[http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/asia-pacific/3506622.stm BBC]</ref>
*[[March 12]] - [[Guantanamo Bay]]: Recently released [[British]] Camp X-Ray inmate Jamal al-Harith is interviewed by the [[Daily Mirror]], alleging physical assaults and psychological torture.<ref>[https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/allnews/content_objectid=14042696_method=full_siteid=50143_headline=-MY%2DHELL%2DIN%2DCAMP%2DX%2DRAY-name_page.html Daily Mirror]</ref><ref>[http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/england/manchester/3504034.stm BBC]</ref>
*[[March 13]]- His Royal Highness [[Prince Richard, Duke of Gloucester|The Duke of Gloucester]] and the Spanish Ambassador to the [[United Kingdom]] attend the Changing of the Guard ceremony at [[Buckingham Palace]] where the Spanish national anthem is played to honour the victims of the Madrid train bombings. The death toll in the bombings rises to 200; investigators continue search for perpetrators, with suspicions against [[Euskadi Ta Askatasuna|ETA]] complemented by the apprehension of five foreign citizens connected to terror attacks in [[Morocco]].<ref>[http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/3509212.stm BBC]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://story.news.yahoo.com/news?tmpl=story&cid=514&e=1&u=/ap/20040313/ap_on_re_eu/spain_bombings_9 |title=Associated Press |access-date=2013-07-09 |archive-date=2005-03-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050306081740/http://story.news.yahoo.com/news?tmpl=story&cid=514&e=1&u=/ap/20040313/ap_on_re_eu/spain_bombings_9 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*[[March 13]] - Fifteen teams that qualified for the DARPA Grand Challenge start on a 150–200 mile robotic race to [[Las Vegas, Nevada]], for a [[United States dollar|$]]1 million prize. All of the teams break down within seven miles of the start line; none collect the prize.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.theregister.co.uk/content/28/36231.html |title=The Register |website=[[The Register]] |access-date=2017-08-21 |archive-date=2008-12-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081205033746/http://www.theregister.co.uk/content/28/36231.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.theregister.co.uk/content/28/36234.html |title=The Register |website=[[The Register]] |access-date=2017-08-21 |archive-date=2008-12-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081205034011/http://www.theregister.co.uk/content/28/36234.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*[[March 13]] - Nine people, including eight [[child]]ren, are found dead in [[Fresno, California]]. One of their family members is arrested for the deaths. The police speculate that the deaths may have been part of a ritual.<ref>[http://www.cnn.com/2004/US/West/03/15/fresno.killings/index.html CNN]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://aolsvc.news.aol.com/news/article.adp?id=20040313025809990001 |title=AOL news |access-date=2013-07-09 |archive-date=2019-08-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190828172650/http://aolsvc.news.aol.com/news/article.adp?id=20040313025809990001 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*[[March 14]] - The Spanish parliamentary elections of 2004 take place. The incumbent government led by [[Jose Maria Aznar]] is defeated by the Socialist [[José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero]].<ref>[http://www.elmundo.es/especiales/2004/03/espana/14m/resultados/congreso/globales/ El Mundo]'''(Spanish)'''</ref><ref>[http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/europe/3511280.stm (BBC)]</ref><ref>[http://www.cnn.com/2004/WORLD/europe/03/14/spain.blasts.election/index.html (CNN)]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.elec_gen04.mir.es/congreso/CGF_TOP.htm |title=(Ministry of Home Affairs) |access-date=2013-07-09 |archive-date=2004-03-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040315104824/http://www.elec_gen04.mir.es/congreso/CGF_TOP.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*[[March 14]] - Two [[suicide bomber]]s kill 10 people in [[Ashdod]], [[Israel]].<ref>[http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/middle_east/3510708.stm BBC]</ref><ref>[http://www.cnn.com/2004/WORLD/meast/03/14/mideast/ CNN]</ref>
*[[March 14]] - [[March 11, 2004 Madrid attacks|Madrid bombings]]: [[Spain|Spanish]] police receives a [[videotape]] where a man identifying himself as an [[al-Qaeda]] spokesman says the organisation claims responsibility for the attack, according to an announcement from the country's interior minister. The authenticity of the video has not been verified. The al-Qaeda claim overshadows voting in the general election.<ref>[http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/3509426.stm BBC]</ref><ref>[http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/europe/3509744.stm BBC]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.thestar.com/NASApp/cs/ContentServer?pagename=thestar%2FLayout%2FArticle_Type1&c=Article&cid=1079265664422&call_pageid=968332188492&col=968793972154 |title=Toronto Star |website=[[Toronto Star]] |access-date=2021-10-05 |archive-date=2011-06-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110606155457/http://www.thestar.com/NASApp/cs/ContentServer?pagename=thestar%2FLayout%2FArticle_Type1&c=Article&cid=1079265664422&call_pageid=968332188492&col=968793972154 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*[[March 14]] - Occupation of Iraq: Six [[United States]] soldiers are killed over the weekend in three separate insurgent roadside bomb attacks, two in [[Baghdad]] and one in [[Tikrit]]. This occurs amidst the largest U.S. troop rotation since [[World War II]].
*[[March 14]] - The people of Russia have a presidential election. Current president [[Vladimir Putin]] wins by a lot of votes. The election is widely criticised by external observers who said Russian state television was very biased towards Putin during the campaign.<ref>[http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/europe/3509412.stm BBC]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.reuters.co.uk/newsPackageArticle.jhtml?type=worldNews&storyID=475555&section=news |title=Reuters |access-date=2013-07-09 |archive-date=2004-08-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040831083144/http://www.reuters.co.uk/newsPackageArticle.jhtml?type=worldNews&storyID=475555&section=news |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*[[March 14]] - [[Pope John Paul II]] becomes the third-longest reigning pope in history, the other two being [[Saint Peter]] and [[Pope Pius IX]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.freep.com/news/religion/pope13_20040313.htm |title=Detroit Free Press |access-date=2013-07-09 |archive-date=2007-09-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070929083336/http://www.freep.com/news/religion/pope13_20040313.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*[[March 14]] - Several [[Kurds]] storm the [[Syrian]] embassy in [[Brussels]] protesting about violence and deaths in north-east Syria over the weekend.<ref>[http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/middle_east/3508710.stm BBC]</ref>
*[[March 14]] - Presidential elections in Russia are held. [[Vladimir Putin]] easily wins a second term.
*[[March 15]] - Four [[United States|U.S.]] [[Baptist]] [[missionary|missionaries]] working on a [[water purification]] project are killed in a drive-by shooting in the northern [[Iraq]]i city of [[Mosul]].<ref>[http://www.cnn.com/2004/WORLD/meast/03/16/iraq.main/index.html CNN]</ref>
*[[March 15]] - The city of [[Aliso Viejo, California]], nearly bans [[Styrofoam|foam]] cups when they learn they are produced from a substance known as [[Water#Dihydrogen monoxide parody|Dihydrogen monoxide]] ([[water]]), a substance that could "threaten human health and safety." <ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.msnbc.msn.com/id/4534017/ |title=MSNBC |access-date=2013-07-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090203192807/http://www.msnbc.msn.com/id/4534017/ |archive-date=2009-02-03 |url-status=dead}}</ref>
*[[March 15]] - [[Pavlo Lazarenko]], former prime minister of [[Ukraine]], stands trial in a U.S. federal court in [[San Francisco]] for [[money laundering]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ktvu.com/news/2923065/detail.html |title=Associated Press |access-date=2013-07-09 |archive-date=2011-09-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927010417/http://www.ktvu.com/news/2923065/detail.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*[[March 15]] - [[Same-sex marriage in the United States]]: Commissioners of [[Multnomah County, Oregon]] dismiss state attorney general Hardy Myers' non-binding opinion that [[same-sex marriage]]s are illegal and vow to continue issuing marriage licenses to [[Homosexual|same-sex]] couples.<ref>[http://seattletimes.nwsource.com/html/localnews/2001879597_weboregaymarriage15.html Seattle Times]</ref>
*[[March 15]] - Newly elected [[Spain|Spanish]] [[Prime Minister]] [[José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero]] announces his government's opposition to the invasion and continued occupation of Iraq and his intention to withdraw Spanish troops from [[Iraq]] by June 30, unless they are part of a [[U.N.]] force.<ref>[http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/europe/3512144.stm BBC]</ref>
*[[March 15]] - Astronomers announce the discovery of Sedna, a [[Pluto (planet)|Pluto]]-like planetoid which is the most distant individual object known to orbit the [[Sun]].<ref>[http://www.gps.caltech.edu/~mbrown/sedna/ Caltech]</ref><ref>[http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/sci/tech/3511678.stm BBC]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.theaustralian.news.com.au/common/story_page/0,5744,8968352%255E29098,00.html |title=The Australian |access-date=2013-07-09 |archive-date=2006-02-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060218144936/http://www.theaustralian.news.com.au/common/story_page/0,5744,8968352%255E29098,00.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*[[March 15]] - Exiled [[Syrian]] [[Kurds]] storm the Syrian consulate in [[Geneva City|Geneva]] and other Kurds protest in Turkey and Germany at weekend violence in northeast Syria.<ref>[http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/europe/3513960.stm BBC]</ref>
*[[March 16]] - [[Spain|Spanish]] police identify six [[Moroccan]]s suspected to have carried out the March 11 Madrid attacks. Five of the suspects are still at large but one is in custody.<ref>[http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/europe/3515138.stm (BBC)]</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/articles/A63338-2004Mar16.html |title=Washington Post |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=2017-08-21 |archive-date=2012-10-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121019201330/http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/articles/A63338-2004Mar16.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

*[[March 16]] - The [[Federal Reserve]] votes to keep interest rates the same, primarily since there are not many new jobs in the United States.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Forbes |website=[[Forbes]] |url=https://www.forbes.com/markets/newswire/2004/03/16/rtr1300749.html |access-date=2017-08-21 |archive-date=2005-02-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050204120644/http://www.forbes.com/markets/newswire/2004/03/16/rtr1300749.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*[[March 17]] - Unrest in Kosovo: After two [[Albania]]n children are found drowned in the [[Ibar river]] in [[Kosovo and Metohia]], with a third still missing, riots erupt in the town of [[Kosovska Mitrovica]] and later spread to the entire province. Mitrovica [[Serbs]] are blamed by Albanian media for forcing the children into the river, but this is later denied by [[United Nations]] officials. At least 22 people are killed by the end of the day with hundreds injured in clashes between Serbs and Albanians; enclaves of Kosovo Serbs elsewhere in the province experience attacks by Kosovo Albanians as well as offices of UN officials which were abandoned. In reaction to the violence in Kosovo, demonstrators in [[Serbia]] march in [[Belgrade]] and set ablaze [[mosque]]s in Belgrade and Nish.<ref>[http://www.b92.net/english/news/index.php?&nav_category=&nav_id=27520&order=priority&style=headlines B92]</ref><ref>[http://www.b92.net/english/news/index.php?&nav_category=&nav_id=27483&order=priority&style=headlines B92]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.swissinfo.org/sen/Swissinfo.html?siteSect=143&sid=4798093 |title=SwissInfo |access-date=2013-07-09 |archive-date=2004-08-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040831085708/http://www.swissinfo.org/sen/Swissinfo.html?siteSect=143&sid=4798093 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2004/03/17/international/europe/17CND-KOSO.html?hp NYT]</ref><ref>[http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/europe/3521068.stm BBC]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cnn.com/2004/WORLD/europe/03/17/kosovo.clash.ap/index.html |title=CNN |website=[[CNN]] |access-date=2013-07-09 |archive-date=2004-04-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040401172134/http://www.cnn.com/2004/WORLD/europe/03/17/kosovo.clash.ap/index.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[http://www.b92.net/english/news/index.php?&nav_category=&nav_id=27517&order=priority&style=headlines B92]</ref><ref>[http://www.rts.co.yu/jedna_vest.asp?source=komentar&IDNews=71242 RTS]{{Dead link|date=January 2021 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} '''(Serbian)'''</ref>
*[[March 17]] - Occupation of Iraq: A [[car bomb]] flattens the Mount Lebanon Hotel in central [[Baghdad]], killing at least 17 people and hurting 45 more people.<ref>[http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/middle_east/3522424.stm BBC]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cnn.com/2004/WORLD/meast/03/17/iraq.main/index.html |title=CNN |website=[[CNN]] |access-date=2013-07-09 |archive-date=2008-12-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081218043118/http://www.cnn.com/2004/WORLD/meast/03/17/iraq.main/index.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.democracynow.org/article.pl?sid=04%2F03%2F18%2F157209 |title=Democracy Now! |website=[[Democracy Now!]] |access-date=2021-10-05 |archive-date=2007-11-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071114124109/http://www.democracynow.org/article.pl?sid=04%2F03%2F18%2F157209 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*[[March 17]] - [[Utah]] bans [[Death penalty|execution by firing squad]].<ref>[http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/americas/3519310.stm BBC]</ref>
*[[March 18]] - [[Howard Dean]] announces plans to form [[Democracy for America]], a political organization intended to help progressive candidates holding similar views.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cnn.com/2004/ALLPOLITICS/03/18/dean.advocacy.ap/index.html |title=CNN |website=[[CNN]] |access-date=2013-07-09 |archive-date=2004-03-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040321123028/http://www.cnn.com/2004/ALLPOLITICS/03/18/dean.advocacy.ap/index.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*[[March 18]] - Unrest in Kosovo: The [[North Atlantic Treaty Organisation]] (NATO) announces that it will reinforce its Kosovo peacekeeping force, following ethnic fighting there that has killed at least 31 people over the past two days. More [[Serbian Orthodox Church]]es have been set on fire by [[Albania]]ns and violence has continued in and around Kosovo Serb enclaves. [[Russia]] and Serbia-Montenegro call for an urgent meeting of the [[UN Security Council]]. United Nations officials attempt to restore order in the province and blame the unrest on nationalist extremists on both sides. More demonstrations have taken place across [[Serbia]], so far without the violence seen the previous day.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/articles/A3832-2004Mar18.html |title=Washington Post |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=2017-08-21 |archive-date=2012-10-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121019201337/http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/articles/A3832-2004Mar18.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/europe/3525168.stm BBC]</ref><ref>[http://www.b92.net/english/news/index.php?order=priority B92]</ref>
*[[March 18]] - [[Near-Earth asteroid]] 2004 FH is making the closest approach of an asteroid ever recorded. At 22:08 UTC it will pass 43,000 km above Earth's surface.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://neo.jpl.nasa.gov/news/news142.html |title=NASA |access-date=2013-07-09 |archive-date=2017-03-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170308130124/http://neo.jpl.nasa.gov/news/news142.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*[[March 18]] - Cleanup work at [[Love Canal]] has been completed, federal officials said. The [[United States Environmental Protection Agency|EPA]] says it should be taken off the [[Superfund]] list.
*[[March 18]] - The [[United States House of Representatives]] all agree to double the reward for [[Osama bin Laden]]'s capture to US$50 million.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cnn.com/2004/ALLPOLITICS/03/18/osama.reward.ap/index.html |title=CNN |website=[[CNN]] |access-date=2013-07-09 |archive-date=2004-04-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040401184240/http://www.cnn.com/2004/ALLPOLITICS/03/18/osama.reward.ap/index.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*[[March 19]] - [[ICANN]] announces that a [[Toronto, Canada]] organization, the International Foundation for Online Responsibility (IFFOR), has applied to sponsor the .xxx [[top-level domain]]. IFFOR claims that a special domain would help stop [[child]]ren from seeing [[pornography]]. However, in February the [[Internet Engineering Task Force]] released <nowiki>RFC 3675</nowiki>, ".sex Considered Dangerous", detailing technical and administrative concerns with such proposals.<ref>[http://thewhir.com/marketwatch/ica032304.cfm Web Host Industry Review]</ref><ref>[http://www.spinics.net/lists/ietf-ann/msg13799.html IETF announcement]</ref><ref>[http://www.icann.org/tlds/stld-apps-19mar04/xxx.htm .xxx application]</ref>
*[[March 19]] - The U.S. military drops all charges of alleged mishandling of [[classified information]] against [[Muslim]] [[Army]] [[chaplain]] Yousef Yee at [[Guantanamo Bay]].<ref>[http://www.foxnews.com/story/0,2933,114716,00.html FOX]</ref>
*[[March 19]] - Same-sex marriage in Canada: The Quebec Court of Appeal upholds a [[Quebec]] superior court ruling that [[same-sex marriage]]s are valid under [[Canada]]'s Charter of Rights and Freedoms.<ref>[http://www.cbc.ca/stories/2004/03/19/gaymarriage040319 CBC]</ref> It joins [[Ontario]] and [[British Columbia]] in permitting same-sex marriage. The couple which brought the suit is scheduled to be wed on [[April 10]], after a required 20-day waiting period.
*[[March 19]] - Äänekoski bus disaster: At least 24 young people are killed and 15 hurt, several of them seriously, in a collision on an icy road between a coach and a [[lorry]] carrying rolls of paper on Highway 4 near [[Äänekoski]] in [[Central Finland]]. The accident happened at around 2 a.m. local time ([[UTC]] +2).<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.helsinki-hs.net/news.asp?id=20040318IE8 |title=Helsingin Sanomat |access-date=2013-07-09 |archive-date=2005-12-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051203121155/http://www.helsinki-hs.net/news.asp?id=20040318IE8 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/3549379.stm BBC]</ref>
*[[March 19]] - The newspaper ''[[USA Today]]'' admits that a former reporter, [[Jack Kelley]], invented or distorted important parts of at least eight major stories.  He was, for example, a finalist for the [[Pulitzer Prize]] in 2001 on the basis of an eyewitness account of a [[suicide bombing]] that, could not have happened as he described it.<ref>[https://www.usatoday.com/news/2004-03-18-2004-03-18_kelleymain_x.htm USA Today]</ref>

Clarke]], claims that Bush diverted attention towards [[Iraq]], ignoring the main threat of [[Al-Qaeda]]. ===April===
*[[April 2]] - A bomb found on the [[Madrid]] to [[Seville]] train line is defused by Spanish police.
*[[April 3]] - A bomb explosion in a Madrid flat kills five suspected terrorists responsible for the Madrid train bombings on March 11, and a Spanish policeman.
*[[April 5]] - Her Majesty Queen [[Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom]] begins a state visit to [[France]] to celebrate the 100th anniversary of the Entente Cordiale
*[[April 8]] - Three [[Japan]]ese [[citizen]]s are taken [[Hostage]] in [[Iraq]].
*[[April 16]] - [[India]] defeats [[Pakistan]] in their historic first [[cricket (sport)|cricket]] tour in 14 years.
*[[April 17]] - [[Israel]]i helicopters fire missiles at a convoy of vechiles in the [[Gaza Strip]], killing the leader of [[Hamas]], Abdel Aziz al-Rantissi
*[[April 20]] - [[Tony Blair]] announces that the UK will hold a [[referendum]] on the European constitution.
*[[April 21]] - Mordechai Vanunu is released from [[prison]] in [[Israel]] after an 18-year term for [[treason]].
*[[April 21]] - The [[United States|American]] TV network, [[CBS]] broadcasts pictures of [[Diana, Princess of Wales]] as she lay dying moments after the fatal car crash that killed her.
*[[April 22]] - Two trains carrying explosives and fuel collide in the [[North Korea]]n town of Ryongchon, killing 161 people, injuring 1,300 and destroying thousands of homes.
*[[April 22]] - The last [[coal]] mine in [[France]] closes, ending nearly 300 years of coal mining.
*[[April 24]] - The christening of [[Lady Louise Windsor]] takes place at [[Windsor Castle]].
*[[April 25]] - [[Cyprus|Greek Cypriots]] reject a United Nations plan to unite the island of Cyprus in a referendum.

===May===
*[[May 1]] - An enlargement of the [[European Union]] takes place, expanding the Union by 10 member-states: [[Poland]], [[Lithuania]], [[Latvia]], [[Estonia]], the [[Czech Republic]], [[Slovakia]], [[Slovenia]], [[Hungary]], [[Malta]], and [[Cyprus]].
*[[May 2]] - After 3 weeks of captivity, American contractor Thomas Hamill escapes from his captors in Iraq with just a gunshot wound to the arm and makes it to US Military personnel.
*[[May 5]] - [[Parliament]] grounds in [[New Zealand]] host 15,000 people protesting about the proposed law that would change the ownership of foreshore and seabed.
*[[May 6]] - The president of [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]], [[Mikhail Saakashvili]], announces that Adzharian leader Aslan Abashidze has left the country, ending a political crisis there.
*[[May 6]] - The final episode of ''[[Friends]]'' airs on [[NBC]]. Advertisers pay $2 million for 30 second ads.
*[[May 9]] - [[Chechnya|Chechen]] president Akhmad Kadyrov is killed by landmine placed under a VIP stage during a [[World War II]] memorial victory parade in [[Grozny]], Chechnya.
*[[May 10]] - Canadian Sponsorship Scandal - The RCMP arrest Chuck Guite and Jean Brault in connection with the scandal.
*[[May 10]] - Final phase of elections to the [[Lok Sabha]] in [[India]]
*[[May 10]] - National election takes place in the [[Philippines]] for the [[President of the Philippines|presidency]] and almost all other elective positions.
*[[May 11]] - Explosion destroys a plastics factory in [[Glasgow]], [[United Kingdom|UK]], killing nine people and injuring over a hundred.
*[[May 11]]  - A [[bomb]] explodes in a crowded market in [[Iraq]]. It kills three people and wounds at least 23.
*[[May 11]]  - [[Chechnya|Chechen]] President Akhmad Kadyrov is buried in his home village.
*[[May 12]] - An American civilian contractor in Iraq, Nick Berg, is shown being decapitated by a group with links to [[al-Qaida]] on a web-distributed video. They state it is retaliation for the abuse at [[Abu Ghraib prison]].
*[[May 12]] - Semi final takes place in the [[Eurovision Song Contest 2004]] in [[Turkey]].
*[[May 13]] - In India, the Congress Party wins a shock victory in the elections to the [[Lok Sabha]] (lower house of [[Parliament of India|Parliament]]).
*[[May 13]] - The season finale for [[Frasier]] is aired.
*[[May 14]] - The editor of the [[Daily Mirror]] newspaper in the UK, [[Piers Morgan]], is sacked after the British army proves photographs in the newspaper, allegedly showing British soldiers abusing Iraqi detainees, to be fake.
*[[May 14]]  - Danish Crown Prince Frederik has married Australian Mary Konadson in [[Copenhagen]], [[Denmark]].
*[[May 15]] - [[Fédération Internationale de Football Association|FIFA]] announces that [[South Africa]] will host the [[2010]] [[FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] [[soccer]] tournament, making it the first African nation to do so.
*[[May 20]] - A [[richter scale|6.5-magnitude]] [[earthquake]] hits [[Taiwan]]. There is no immediate reports of damage or injuries.

===June===
*[[June 5]] - Former U.S. President [[Ronald Reagan]] dies of [[pneumonia]] at the age of 93.
*[[June 11]] - [[State funeral of Ronald Reagan|state funeral]] of former U.S. President [[Ronald Reagan]] is held.
*[[June 12]] - Former U.S. President [[George H. W. Bush|George H.W. Bush]] celebrates his 80th birthday by [[skydiving]].

===July===
*[[July 1]] – The [[Cassini-Huygens]] spacecraft arrives at [[Saturn (planet)|Saturn]].
*[[July 4]] – Groundbreaking for the Freedom Tower begins at [[Ground Zero]] in [[New York City]].
*[[July 4]] – In football, [[Greece]] wins the [[Europe]]an Championships, after being rated as an 80-1 rank outsider.

===August===
*[[August 13]]–[[August 29]] – The [[2004 Summer Olympics]] are held in [[Athens]], [[Greece]].
*[[August 16]] – The village of [[Boscastle]] in [[Cornwall]] is hit by a flash flood.

===September===
*[[September 1]] – Many schoolchildren are taken hostage at a school in Beslan, southern [[Russia]]. Many of them are massacred on [[September 3]].
*[[September 23]] – [[Mount St. Helens]] becomes active again.

===October===
*[[October 27]] – The [[Boston Red Sox]] sweep the [[St. Louis Cardinals]] in four games to win the 2004 World Series.  It is the Red Sox first World Series championship since 1918.
*[[October 29]] – King [[Norodom Sihanouk]] of [[Cambodia]] abdicates in favour of his son, [[Norodom Sihamoni]].

===November===
*[[November 2]] – [[George W. Bush]] is reelected as [[President of the United States]].  He defeats [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] senator [[John Kerry]].
*[[November 21]] – The [[Orange Revolution]] begins in [[Ukraine]].

===December===
*[[December 26]] - A strong [[2004 Indian Ocean earthquake|earthquake from the Indian Ocean]] kills at least 140,000 people.
*[[December 26]] – In the wake of the [[Orange Revolution]], [[Viktor Yushchenko]] is elected [[President]] of [[Ukraine]].
*[[December 31]] – The [[Taipei 101]] tower is opened in [[Taipei]], [[Taiwan]].

text:
{{more sources|date=December 2013}} {{Infobox mountain|name=Mauna Loa|elevation_ft=13,679|prominence_ft=7,079|photo=Mauna Loa Volcano.jpg|coordinates={{coord|19|28|46|N|155|36|10|W|}}|map=USA Hawaii|map_caption=Mauna Loa within the Hawaiian Islands|type=[[Shield volcano]]|last_eruption=2022|volcanic_arc=[[Hawaiian–Emperor seamount chain]]|location=[[Hawaii (island)|Hawaii County]], [[Hawaii]], [[United States]]|language=[[Hawaiian language|Hawaiian]]}}
[[File:Mauna Loa erupting at night, 1984.jpg|thumb|right|Mauna Loa was releasing lava in 1984]]
'''Mauna Loa''' is an [[active volcano]] on [[Hawaii Island]], in the state of [[Hawaii]], United States. It is considered to be the largest subaerial (from the bottom of the [[Pacific Ocean]]) volcano in the world and the tallest volcano in Hawaii.

== Name ==
''Mauna Loa'' is [[Hawaiian language|Hawaiian]] for "long mountain."

==Size==
The [[volcano]] is at least {{convert|18000|mi3|km3}} in volume<ref>{{cite conference|last=Kaye|first=G.D.|title=Using GIS to estimate the total volume of Mauna Loa Volcano, Hawaii|url=http://gsa.confex.com/gsa/2002CD/finalprogram/abstract_34712.htm|book-title=98th Annual Meeting|conference=Geological Society of America|year=2002|access-date=2009-10-26|archive-date=2009-01-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090125194545/http://gsa.confex.com/gsa/2002CD/finalprogram/abstract_34712.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> and over 4 kilometers above sea level.  Measured from its base on the ocean floor, it reaches above 8 kilometers, making it the tallest mountain on Earth,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mauna Loa|url=https://www.volcanodiscovery.com/maunaloa.html|access-date=2020-08-11|website=www.volcanodiscovery.com|archive-date=2020-06-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200609101015/https://www.volcanodiscovery.com/maunaloa.html|url-status=live}}</ref> but not the highest. That distinction is reserved for [[Mount Everest]]. 

Measured from sea level Mauna Loa is 4,169 meters high.<ref>Kaye, G.D. [http://gsa.confex.com/gsa/2002CD/finalprogram/abstract_34712.htm  "Using GIS to estimate the total volume of Mauna Loa Volcano, Hawaii,"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090125194545/http://gsa.confex.com/gsa/2002CD/finalprogram/abstract_34712.htm |date=2009-01-25 }} ''Geological Society of America, 98th Annual Meeting''; retrieved 2012-6-18.</ref> It is also one of the largest volcanoes measuring 96 kilometers long and 48 kilometers wide.  

The world's biggest volcano is named Mauna Loa in Hawaii. Mauna Loa is part of the five volcanoes on Hawaii Island. The most recent time this volcano erupted was in 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Mauna Loa|url=https://www.nps.gov/havo/learn/nature/ml2022.htm|access-date=April 18, 2025|website=National Park Service}}</ref> It erupted 33 times in the last 170 years. Like all the other Hawaiian volcanoes, Mauna Loa was created by the movement of the [[Pacific tectonic plate]] which moved over the Hawaii [[hotspot (geology)|hotspot]] in the Earth's mantle. It is a shield volcano. The largest recent eruption from Mauna Loa left a [[lava]] trail 51 kilometers long.
